### LLM Applicability And Mutation Dimensions

| Contract | Exact identity dimensions | Mutation/invalidation and publication boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Active judgment source | `app.judgment` article ID, prompt ID, model ID, `use_title`, `use_abstract`, `use_fulltext`, `use_fulltext_no_images`; `deleted_at IS NULL`; latest `created_at,id`; physical uniqueness also includes `delete_generation`. | LLM create/update/delete deltas carry article, prompt, judgment, model and all four flags. Delete-generation behavior differs across writers as frozen by `BLK-0117`; a deleted-at-only mutation is not equivalent to a generation bump. |
| Current review hash | Project model ID; provider connection ID/kind/base URL; remote model ID; variant; full model execution options including thinking; Human mode; ordered enabled/nonarchived prompt ID/order/config hash; four content flags. | Project/prompt/model/provider helpers emit config deltas, but model/provider display/enabled/auth/secret and some broader metadata dimensions remain outside or differently represented. The hash is a projection/snapshot identity, not proof of active-judgment natural identity. |
| Projected LLM status | Current project prompt set plus latest active judgment under model ID and four flags; answered when persisted `is_answered`, scalar answer, or nonempty array is present; article answered only when all enabled prompts are answered. | Status dirty/full paths directly update candidate/active serving rows and can report zero physical patch rows. Status, count, payload and claim acknowledgement remain distinct. |
| Judgment detail payload | Current project prompts and the same model/four-flag active judgment selection. Relational row stores model ID; JSON embeds current model/provider/display/options-thinking metadata and prompt/assessment/quote content at projection time. | `review_config_hash` and snapshot bind applicability indirectly; detail rows do not persist the four flags or provider/variant/options as relational identity. Later model metadata projection can differ from judgment natural identity. |
| Display/selected import | Project scope, selected-import snapshot/winner, canonical article, current source link/record and metadata; independent of model/content applicability. | Article/import/scope/config mutations invalidate different component slices. Selected-import base can mutate under a completed snapshot and final candidate fields can publish under another component. |
| Route and client | Route re-resolves current review hash and active/LKG manifest; list cursor binds that snapshot. The later UI count query has its own cache and manifest resolution. | No route silently changes model/content flags. Source does not prove that a five-minute count, displayed page, detail navigation, export/job snapshot, and later active config share one applicability identity. |

### Human Source, Status And Mutation Contracts

| Contract | Exact identity and semantics | Mutation/publication boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prompt Human source | `app.judgment_human` ID plus nullable project, article and prompt; persisted `is_answered`, nullable answer/comment and timestamps. Pending init creates `is_answered=false`; submit sets true even for optional blank answers. | Status projector calls blank unanswered; detail JSON copies persisted `is_answered`; summary contribution accepts JSON `isAnswered`; nonblank-only delta/overlay means optional blank can miss incremental projection. |
| Summary Human source | `app.judgment_human_summary` project/article identity, nullable yes/no/maybe answer, origin `covidence_import` or `manual_override`, timestamps; synthetic prompt ID `summary`. | Covidence origin is projected/serialized answered even with null answer, but list/detail/facet/posting paths independently include, exclude, or label that null row. |
| Review mode | Current project mode participates in review hashing and chooses prompt-versus-summary status, payload source, posting, facets/options and detail response interpretation. | Existing prompt and summary rows are not migrated by a mode change. Mode delta/rebuild, comparison invalidation, source retention and empty-page/client interpretation remain separate. |
| Human delta | All current Human create/update/delete-style events that emit use `change_kind='judgment.human.updated'`, typed project/article/Human key and optional prompt; source operation/payload can differ. | Some pending, prompt replacement/merge, archived cleanup and blank-submit mutations emit no Human delta or old-identity tombstone. A delete source operation is not a distinct delete change kind. |
| Reviewer overlay | Nonblank mounted submit writes a deterministic pending row overlay bound to review config, source partition/high-water and `read_surface='row'`. | Append is production-wired; read/reconcile/expire helpers have no non-test caller, no Human route consumes it, and retention does not register the table. It currently does not establish read-your-write. |
| Comparison invalidation | Mounted submit marks comparison stale for every submitted prompt row; other Human writers have writer-specific or absent comparison handling. | Comparison invalidation is neither the Human delta nor review-serving convergence. Prompt merges/deletes, import/clone/transfer and mode transitions need their own parity proof. |
| Serving publication | Human status directly updates candidate rows; Human payload replaces detail; posting, summary/facets and options publish in separate component/request phases; candidate promotion validates component state later. | A component can acknowledge/advance while another Human representation is stale. Patch row count zero, component success, finalization and active snapshot are independent. |

### Mounted Both Response And Client Field Closure

| Field family | Exact API fields and transform | Serving/source closure | Current client use and boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Envelope, order and cursor | `data`, `totalCount`, `page`, `limit`, `totalPages`, `nextCursor`; candidate rows use `sort_key DESC, article_id ASC`, `limit+1`, page slice, then cursor from the last returned row only when an extra row exists. Numeric page values without a cursor collapse to page one. | Candidate `CMF-1084`-`CMF-1127`; cursor binds review hash, snapshot, filter signature and component state. | The table accumulates pages/cursors and uses the embedded total for header, pagination and select-all. It starts no separate Both count query and retains prior page IDs until filter reset. |
| Article, import and payload | Common scalar response includes internal/external IDs, title/timestamps, journal, URL, identifiers, PDF fields, selected import route and parsed `sourceMetadata`. `canonicalArticleId` and `originalData` survive the transform but are absent from current selected mart columns; broader metadata fields in `ArticleReviewsBothResult` are not emitted. | Shared `LIN-0003`-`LIN-0005`, `LIN-0010`, `LIN-0017`; candidate/payload `CMF-1098`-`CMF-1119`, `CMF-1195`-`CMF-1205`, `CMF-1250`-`CMF-1252`. | Title/link, dates, display identifier, journal, PDF and Covidence badges are consumed. All review-table titles route through the LLM detail path. Type presence and shared source are not browser/desktop rendering or navigation proof. |
| Membership and statuses | Request supplies no status or Human mode. Service injects LLM `complete`, translated to persisted `answered`, plus Human `answered`; neither candidate status key nor projected count is serialized. | Candidate `CMF-1120`-`CMF-1124`; LLM and Human status projectors independently mutate the `both` row. | Header copy says complete LLM and Human judgments for all prompts. The UI has no displayed shared status field and cannot verify the two projected predicates from the response. |
| LLM judgments | `judgments[].{id,createdAt,articleId,promptId,modelId,answeredOriginal,answeredOriginalAsArray,explanation,quotes}`; placeholder rows are removed. | LLM source `CMF-0209`-`CMF-0230` -> Both detail `CMF-1206`-`CMF-1220`, JSON `CMF-1253`-`CMF-1261` -> bounded post-limit hydration. | Prompt mode renders at most three LLM-led comparisons and a `+N` count. Labels use scalar/array values, but tone compares only normalized scalar `answeredOriginal`. IDs, model, explanation and quotes are ignored. |
| Human prompt composition | When no hydrated `prompt_id='summary'` exists, route sets `humanJudgmentMode:'prompt'` and groups every non-null Human answer into `humanAnswersByPrompt[promptId]`; raw Human judgment rows are not returned. | Prompt source `CMF-0231`-`CMF-0239` -> Human Both detail/JSON `CMF-1206`-`CMF-1220`, `CMF-1262`, `CMF-1263`. | UI iterates only the first three LLM judgments, labels all Human answers for each matching prompt, and computes match/mixed/mismatch from exact lowercased values. Human-only prompts and extra LLM prompts are not rendered individually. |
| Summary composition | Presence of a Human `summary` detail row selects summary mode. Human answer accepts only exact `yes`, `no`, `maybe`; LLM summary normalizes each scalar prompt answer, then returns null for none, otherwise `no`, else `maybe`, else `yes`. | Summary Human source `CMF-0240`-`CMF-0246`; LLM/Human Both detail rows above. Criteria disposition and LLM array answers do not participate in this route reduction. | UI shows one AI/H pair and computes neutral/match/mixed/mismatch; any side missing is neutral and `maybe` disagreement is mixed. This tone is not persisted or returned. |
| Conflict observations | Request `hasStudyDecisionConflict` filters candidate `conflict_flag`; badges read merged Covidence metadata; named `review.both.conflictByPrompt` counts exact scalar prompt inequalities; UI tones normalize and add mixed/neutral categories. | Selected import/candidate `CMF-0857`-`CMF-0872`, `CMF-1118`, payload JSON, detail rows, named count `CMF-1304`-`CMF-1315`. | The checkbox is labeled Covidence conflicts. The page never requests named disagreement counts and does not expose a conflict-only control for its client tone. None of the four observations proves another. |

A matching number does not freeze membership, prove worker order, or equate article count with prompt disagreements. |

### Both Applicability, Ownership And Conflict Contracts

| Contract | Exact identity and semantics | Ownership, invalidation and publication boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Persisted Both candidate | Display base cross-joins every in-scope article with `llm`, `human`, `both`, `unassessed`; `list_mode_key='both'` therefore means a materialized view copy, not assessed-by-both membership. | Display/selected-import owners create the copy. LLM and Human status owners mutate it later; the mounted row and direct-count predicates impose actual membership. |
| LLM applicability | Latest active judgment is selected by article, prompt, model ID and four content flags; status requires every current enabled prompt answered. Review hash additionally includes provider connection/kind/base URL, remote model, variant, thinking/options, ordered prompt hashes and Human mode. | LLM delta starts at `llmStatus`, then queue/payload/posting/summary. Delete generation and writer coverage remain separate from review hashing and Both mode. |
| Human applicability | Current project Human mode chooses prompt rows or summary rows. Prompt status requires all enabled prompt answers nonblank; Covidence summary origin can be answered with null. | Human-updated delta starts at `humanStatus`, then queue/payload/posting/summary. Persisted `is_answered`, projected status, payload JSON and route mode inference remain distinct. |
| Route-time intersection | Reader and direct count require the same snapshot/config/list mode plus `llm_status_key='answered'` and `human_status_key='answered'`; optional date/import/search/LLM-answer predicates further reduce membership. | `review.both.rows` is direct; `review.both.rowsByArticleSet` is mapped-only. Direct count repeats predicates outside the reader, so equality and same-snapshot behavior remain owner contracts. |
| Post-limit composition | LLM and Human detail rows are written and hydrated as separate payload kinds under list mode `both`, then joined only in route memory by article and prompt. | Payload projector owns persisted detail; route owns grouping, mode inference and summary reduction; UI owns tone. There is no persisted combined answer or conflict-tone row. |
| Conflict semantics | Import `conflict_flag`, merged Covidence badge metadata, scalar `conflictByPrompt`, prompt tone and summary tone have different inputs, normalization, units and consumers. | Selected-import, payload, summary projector and UI own separate products. The shared filter page exposes LLM answer choices, not disagreement choices. |
| Mutation, overlay and comparison invalidation | No `both` delta exists. LLM and Human mutation families independently invalidate review serving. Human nonblank submit may append a row overlay; selected LLM/Human writers separately stale comparison-project serving. | Both list consumes candidate/detail snapshots only. It reads neither reviewer overlay nor comparison serving, so neither path establishes combined read-your-write or Both convergence. |

### Queue Eligibility, Prompt Applicability And Physical Identity

| Contract | Source-defined membership and priority | Boundary that remains separate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Project and snapshot | Queue source begins with current `mart.project_scope_article` route/direct membership, selected-import tombstone state, the candidate review hash/snapshot and current project model, four content flags and Human mode. Readers may admit active or LKG; job consumers require active. | Scope materialization, selected-import publication, queue publication and active promotion are distinct transactions. A current hash or manifest status is not a claim-time execution snapshot. |
| LLM `unassessed` | Cross product of scoped articles and enabled, nonarchived project/prompt rows. Latest active judgment by article/prompt and exact current model/four flags is selected by created time then ID. No judgment gives priority `0` and scope activity; an existing unanswered judgment gives priority `1` and judgment creation time. Answered scalar/array/`is_answered`, selected-import or scope tombstones remove it. | Descending consumers put bucket `1` before `0`, but scheduler `filterAlreadyJudged` excludes any matching active judgment without testing answer fields. Queue priority and actual SQLite admission therefore differ. |
| Human `human-unreviewed` | Prompt mode uses enabled/nonarchived prompt links; summary mode synthesizes prompt ID `summary`. No Human timestamp gives priority `0`; any prompt/summary update gives `1`. Nonblank answer or Covidence summary origin tombstones the pair. | The formula ignores prompt-row `is_answered`. Optional blank submit can remain queue-eligible after recomputation, while init's existing-work query excludes it because `is_answered=TRUE`. |
| Stable versus physical identity | Stable JSON identity is `{promptId,queueKind,reviewConfigHash}`. Final `DBO-0155` key additionally contains project, snapshot, priority, activity and article. Incremental work deletes affected article/prompt/range before insert. | Full SQL deduplicates only the complete physical key. Multiple source variants with the same stable logical identity but different priority/activity are not excluded by the physical constraint, and named counts count physical rows. |
| Prompt applicability after queue selection | Normal list has no prompt filter. Job consumers rejoin current enabled/nonarchived prompts. Human init's queue selection uses queue-projector applicability, but response/pending sync loads every project prompt link without enabled/archive predicates. | Queue prompt set, response prompt set, pending-row set and job prompt set can diverge. No persisted prompt-set version or reviewer claim freezes them. |

### Count, Priority, Order, Cursor And Client Contracts

| Surface | Grain/count | Order/cursor | Exactness and consumer boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Normal Unassessed page | Candidate articles having at least one `unassessed` queue pair; each row serializes empty judgment arrays and `isFullyJudged:false`. | Candidate `activity_sort_at DESC, article_id DESC`, `limit+1`; queue priority/activity does not order the page. | With no effective dates or user filters, total reads named prompt-pair contributions. Any date/duplicate/conflict/search filter uses direct `COUNT(DISTINCT article_id)`. UI labels both as an article total and uses it for pagination/select-all. |
| Registered queue reader | Queue pairs for caller-selected kind, max 100. | `priority_bucket, activity_sort_at, article_id, prompt_id, queue_identity` all descending. | Human init is its only current direct caller. Declared filters exceed emitted SQL; date SQL references absent queue column `article_created_at`, though init supplies no user dates. |
| Job count | Distinct eligible `unassessed` article IDs; current prompts, configured route IDs or direct membership, route-context dates, current config and active snapshot. | No order. Optional ten-second cache is admitted by separate legacy project-mart freshness. | UI drops freshness fields, converts absent/falsy to zero, and labels it “DuckDB/project-mart count” although the count SQL reads V4 queue/candidate serving. |
| Job preview | At most 100 grouped articles; returned array length is the only displayed count. | Per article: maximum priority DESC, maximum activity among that priority DESC, article ID DESC. No cursor/total/LKG. | Truncation is not surfaced; returned authors/source/URL fields are null. Thirty-second polling and actual rendering are source intent only. |
| Worker source page | Prompt pairs, max 5,000 plus one probe, with current job/project/prompt/date/route-or-direct scope and active snapshot. | Priority DESC, millisecond-truncated activity DESC, article DESC, prompt DESC; cursor has those four dimensions and omits queue identity. | Rows tied after millisecond truncation and prompt identity lack a strict physical tie-break. The SQL repeats the current-project scope predicate; repetition does not add a fence. |
| Scheduler/SQLite | One source window, max 128 and one window per one-second source-defined tick; canonical/local-judged filters; stable Human-first partition; insert deficit. | Source cursor advances from the fetched page. New rows receive monotonic `ready_insert_seq`; claims use `ready_insert_seq ASC,id ASC`. | In prompt mode, a matching Human row with `is_answered=TRUE`, including blank, promotes that pair; in summary mode, any nonblank summary answer promotes every article prompt. This intake-time stable partition preserves source order within each group, while existing ready rows stay ahead. Exhaustion persists, cools down 60 seconds, then starts a new epoch; it is not an exact fill-to-deficit pass. |

### Writes, Removal, Reprioritization And Read-Your-Write

| Mutation family | Queue effect when downstream work completes | Durability/exactness boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Job LLM completion/import | Local completion/outbox is durable before canonical visibility. Central import inserts or reuses generation-zero identity, appends created deltas per currently visible project, immediately intakes their ranges to dirty work, and later queue recomputation tombstones answered rows or assigns priority `1` to unanswered rows. | Canonical transaction and local outbox acknowledgement are separate. Import markers make central replay idempotent by job/outbox sequence, but duplicate-identity delta, delete-generation and import-to-active-snapshot acknowledgement authority remain unresolved. |
| Other LLM writes/deletes/moves | Direct mutable writer, invalid-answer delete, admin unexpected-answer delete, project prompt cleanup and prompt merge can add, remove or move source identity and thus queue pairs. | Generation bump, project fan-out, delta, comparison invalidation, direct dirty work and recovery differ by caller. No one path proves exhaustive add/remove/reprioritization. |
| Human init/pending sync | Creates missing unanswered prompt rows and deletes stale unanswered rows. New rows can change Human queue priority from `0` to `1` after a later delta-driven recomputation only if an event exists. | Pending create/drift delete emits no Human delta, dirty work, overlay or comparison invalidation, so no operating queue-reprioritization path is proven. Existing pending resume bypasses current queue/scope. |
| Human submit | Every selected row becomes `is_answered=TRUE`; nonblank rows emit Human-updated delta/row overlay and later tombstone the Human queue; all submitted rows stale comparison serving. | Optional blank rows emit no delta/overlay and remain eligible under the queue's nonblank-answer formula. The client refetches only Human init; list/job queries are not explicitly invalidated, and no Human queue/list reader consumes the overlay. |
| Human import/edit/merge/delete | Covidence, clone, transfer, project replacement, prompt merge and archived cleanup can insert, move or hard-delete Human source rows. | Event kind, old/new key, delete tombstone, comparison invalidation, transaction/recovery and retention coverage vary. Unsupported convergence and disposal remain unresolved. |

### Snapshot, Recovery, Restart And Retention Contracts

| Contract | Source-observed behavior | Unsupported inference preserved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Serving publication | Queue incremental writer commits final-row delete/upsert with claim acknowledgement, component manifest and watermark. Full queue chunks write ranges. Summary direct/chunk output, request-wide reduction/options, candidate validation and promotion occur later. | A zero patch count, completed queue component or promoted snapshot does not prove count finalization, one transaction, same-snapshot route reads, exactly-once replay or immutable component state. |
| Human selection exactness | Queue pair read and row-by-set read are separate; row-by-set deliberately omits queue recheck. Pending synchronization is a later transaction. Existing work reads raw article state without manifest admission. | No queue claim, per-reviewer ownership, common snapshot, compare-and-set, retry journal or same-request read-your-write proof exists. Rejected and empty reads collapse to the same 404. |
| Job execution snapshot | Source page uses current project/config/scope; local identity is job/article/prompt; Human-first priority is computed before insert. Execution snapshots are created only while claiming ready rows and written with claim identity. | Source review hash, intake-time Human facts, local ready row and claim-time execution snapshot are not one frozen identity. Equality during edits, restart, replay or concurrent promotion is unproven. |
| Restart/recovery | Server startup recovers stale local leases, flushes preserved completion evidence, discards ready/claimed/running/sent rows for active auto-drain statuses, resets scan state, then drains or fails those jobs. It does not resume the pre-restart ready queue. | Lease recovery, evidence preservation and deterministic discard do not certify queue continuation, ordering parity, no lost work, cross-host failover or deployed recovery. |
| Serving retention/startup probe | Every eligible worker cleanup interval defaults to 60 seconds; at most 16 scopes rotate one of 11 final targets and delete at most 512 rows per target while protecting active/LKG/pins. Queue startup probe changes/restores one `queue_updated_at`. | The probe is not crash-safe restore proof. Final-table retention omits deltas, dirty/control rows, summary partials/accumulators and local job state; bounded calls do not prove full sweep or physical deletion. |
| Local job retention | Source cron patterns run queue intake every second and stale cleanup at `0 */1 * * * *`. Visibility-acked exported outbox rows and judged queue rows prune in bounded batches; draining paths repeat until stable, checkpoint, mark drained and delete SQLite/WAL/SHM/lease files. | Source patterns do not prove deployed single ownership or cadence. Visibility uses legacy project-mart dirty-token acknowledgement rather than V4 queue watermark; no approved deployed shape, retained-history horizon, backup or restore drill exists. |

`cardinality` is `COUNT(*)` over physical posting rows for one
`(filter_kind,filter_value,list_mode_key)`. Full-refresh `selectivity` divides
that count by active `mart.project_scope_article` membership, not by a
route-specific candidate, status, prompt, or searched denominator. Actual
values, fan-out, optimizer use, rows scanned, bytes and pre/post selectivity
remain unavailable because no approved immutable physical fixture was used.

keys, all four list modes, review mode, search identity and summary definition
versions. The Human identity uses seven keys and `human,both`. Route query
date/duplicate/conflict/search values do not enter current identity
construction, and production option refresh does not pass `searchTitle`.

## US-045 Detail, Prompt, Full-Text, And Payload Lineage

US-045 separates candidate-selection facts from detail-only hydration at commit
`d8e2278bac1d3232f6031820297da898acb0f2fb`. A field being stored in a
snapshot table, physically joined before a limit, returned by a route, or
included in an archive is recorded as a distinct fact. None of those facts is
used as deletion authority or as proof of current browser, desktop, deployed,
or physical behavior.

| Prohibited evidence | No live/current DuckDB, configured snapshot/query/studio, server/app/desktop shell, browser, worker, projector, rebuild, promotion, cleanup, migration, transfer, export, full-text fetch/conversion, benchmark, physical profile or product-data mutation ran. |
| State and disposition | Fifteen new `LIN-####` rows use only US-001 `auditStatus`. `proofCheckState`, `recommendationActionability`, `overallCertification`, every definition and every storage disposition remain separate and unchanged. Unsupported homes remain unresolved. |

### Selection, Detail, And Stored-Field Placement

| Field family | Source -> transform -> keyed home | Pre-limit role | Post-limit/detail role | Snapshot/lifecycle boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Display identity and scope | Current project/config/component identities plus project-scope and selected-import facts -> list-mode fan-out -> `DBO-0140` PK `(project,config,snapshot,listMode,article)` | Identity predicates and list-mode scope select the candidate set. | Identity is not rendered; it binds payload/status/summary joins. | Fixed to the written serving snapshot; component identities remain separately mutable until publication. |
| Candidate membership/order | Scope article, selected import, status projectors and summary counters -> `sort_key`, activity, statuses, prompt counts, duplicate/conflict and article ID in `DBO-0140` | Date/status/duplicate/conflict, posting/search intersections, cursor and sort run before page `LIMIT`. | Returned rows drive list labels and later article-ID hydration. | Snapshot-fixed copy; invalidated by the corresponding scope/import/article/judgment/config delta families. |
| Candidate display facts | Title, external IDs, journal, URL, PDF/fetched/conversion display state, rank/year and opened/section counters -> `DBO-0140` | Physically read with candidates but not all fields are membership/order predicates. | Current list clients consume a subset after the page is selected. | Snapshot copy; source updates do not become visible until a replacement snapshot is read. |
| Payload identity/order | Display/payload identities, snapshot, article ID and article-created time -> `DBO-0151` PK `(project,display,payload,snapshot,article)` | Prompt preview orders by article-created time; list SQL physically left-joins the payload row before its candidate predicates and limit. | Keyed detail/export reads and list `source_metadata` serialization occur after logical candidate selection. | Same snapshot key as the candidate join, but payload is a separately written component. |
| Abstract/full-text preview | `app.article.article_summary` and full text or HTML stripped of tags -> `LEFT(...,2000)` -> `abstract_text`, `full_text_preview` | Neither value is a list membership, filter, cursor or order input. | Detail payload, prompt candidate preview and CSV abstract use them. Project detail can replace the preview with current full text. | Snapshot-truncated copies; not the canonical full text and not a frozen current-article read. |
| Source metadata | Canonical/selected-import source metadata -> JSON copy in `DBO-0151` | Physically joined before list limit but no current membership/order predicate uses it. | Selected list rows, detail and CSV may expose it; current global/transfer paths can instead read broader app/raw metadata. | Snapshot copy with an open JSON value domain; nested legacy keys remain unresolved. |
| Payload bytes | Lengths of source summary/full text/full-text HTML/canonical metadata/selected-import metadata -> nonnegative aggregate -> `payload_bytes` | No selection predicate or client control uses it. | Contract/diagnostic budget input only; it is not the byte length of the two 2,000-character stored previews. | Snapshot diagnostic; equality to encoded output bytes and deployed values are unavailable. |
| Judgment relational fields | Latest applicable LLM or current-mode Human rows -> kind/list-mode fan-out -> prompt/order, judgment/model, scalar/array answer and placeholder columns in `DBO-0152` | Prompt-answer/status projectors can derive separate candidate/posting facts; list membership does not read arbitrary JSON payload keys. | Article-ID-bounded hydration orders/deduplicates by article, prompt and list-mode priority. | Snapshot copy keyed by project/config/snapshot/listMode/kind/article/prompt. |
| LLM detail JSON | Current prompt + latest active judgment/assessment + current model/provider metadata -> named serializer in `EVD-0493` | Not a candidate sort field; separate relational/status/posting facts drive selection. | Assessments, explanation, confidence, quotes, model identity/thinking/version, content snapshots, placeholders and prompt display hydrate detail/list/CSV. | Snapshot payload; JSON/relational equality and dynamic metadata domains remain unresolved. |
| Human detail JSON | Current prompt + current-mode prompt/summary Human judgment -> named serializer in `EVD-0493` | Not a candidate sort field; Human status/prompt postings are separate. | Answer/comment/times/reference/prompt display hydrate detail/list/CSV. | Snapshot payload; prompt-versus-summary mode and blank/answered semantics remain separately governed. |
| Canonical full text/admin | `DBO-0001` keyed article row: full text/HTML/PDF/assets, source/original format, fetched time, conversion status/error/attempt/model/metadata/char count | Keyed after a selected article or direct global/article ID; not required for list membership. | Project/global full-text tabs, preview processing, admin polling, conversion and transfer serialization. | Current mutable app state; no review snapshot, response byte cap or common read pin. |
| Physical assets | Article PDF/HTML/asset references -> rooted `DBO-0304`, `DBO-0305`, `DBO-0313`, runtime root `DBO-0322` | References may be copied into a candidate row; file bytes are never a list predicate. | Runtime route, conversion, transfer export/import and browser/desktop download resolve after selection. | File and reference writes are separate; existence, checksum, cleanup, retained copy and platform parity remain unresolved. |

The payload join in `buildReviewServingRowsSql` is physically before
`WHERE`, `ORDER BY` and `LIMIT`, so its scan/cost is pre-limit. That placement
does not make abstract, full-text preview, source metadata or payload bytes
logical candidate-selection inputs. No approved physical fixture or plan was
used to measure the join, so storage necessity and cost remain unresolved.

| Prompt preview | Earliest payload by article-created time/article ID, max one; separate keyed detail row max one. | Optional current full text is one row with no byte cap, then model token limiting/image stripping occurs before prompt builders. | Payload/detail/config/model/full text have no common snapshot; generated prompt strings are response-only and not persisted. | Toggle-gated 60-second query; UI ignores diagnostics and system/user strings; no browser/desktop capture. |
| Global article detail | Direct article ID, at most one article. | Full broad article and all judgment history have no aggregate byte/row cap; optional project-name hydration follows. | Entirely current app state with no manifest/LKG/snapshot. | Two tabs share a five-minute query key; exact cache/navigation/full-text/PDF behavior is unavailable. |

| Project CSV | Durable result manifest bounds membership to stored article IDs; download processes sequential 500-ID batches. | Serving article/detail reads are article-ID bounded, but aggregate CSV bytes/rows are not enforced by the declared 10 MB budget. | Pinned scopes can fix serving rows; latest scopes are re-resolved at download. Authors/raw selected-source payload remain current. No server CSV file is retained. | Client direct-fetches/polls and then downloads a stream; saved-file integrity, object lifetime and platform parity are unavailable. |
| Prompt CSV | Request-selected prompt IDs; current prompt read. | No explicit aggregate byte/order snapshot cap. | Response stream only; no durable server artifact/checksum. | Client blob/object URL/temporary anchor path applies to both, but save/cleanup was not executed. |
| Transfer export | Current project scope; database payload rows are captured inside one transaction. | Serializer includes bounded package/member/depth/ratio/resource checks; full text is conditional, while HTML/PDF/assets/admin fields are included. | Database rows are transaction-fixed, assets are copied later, and completed package bytes are checksum/fingerprint fixed. Ready packages expire after 24 hours; no download lease. | Shared page supports inline blob or queued polling/download; integrity headers are not validated by a captured client flow. |
| Transfer import | Manifest/session identity plus analyzed plan; asset promotion uses exclusive create and byte/hash checks. | Promoted references are rewritten before one app/history transaction; reused articles fill only missing fields. | Failed work rolls back owned assets; success retains promoted assets without an independent horizon. Temp/session cleanup is state/expiry based. | Imported references become runtime-asset eligible under the target runtime root; no browser/desktop load or restore validation ran. |

No source-backed home was found for a persisted prompt-preview response,
route-composed project/global detail envelope, generated server CSV, browser
download receipt, desktop saved-copy ledger, runtime-PDF lease/checksum, or
complete successful promoted-asset retention record. These absences remain
unsupported homes under `BLK-0192`-`BLK-0196`; they are not deletion or
implementation authority.

## US-046 Warning, Health, Readiness, And Progress Lineage

US-046 traces diagnostic and progress fields at commit
`395b8e2b3e450e75aacd58ac70aefeab9507109a`. Transport success, semantic
readiness, mutable control-plane observations, repair mutation, durable job
progress, projector publication, startup recovery, retention and actual
browser/desktop behavior remain separate contracts. Source-defined intervals
and query keys are recorded, but they are not treated as measured request
counts, deduplication or physical cost.

### US-046 Evidence Boundary

| Boundary | Recorded result |
| --- | --- |
| Source identity | Commit `395b8e2b3e450e75aacd58ac70aefeab9507109a`; Ralph's pre-existing timestamp-only `tasks/prd.json` modification remains untouched. |
| Prerequisite | US-045 is complete. US-021 warning/health/progress, US-026 browser diagnostics, US-030 desktop diagnostics, US-031 desktop execution, and US-035-US-045 serving/lifecycle rows remain authoritative and are refined rather than replaced. |
| Allowed evidence | Exact route composition, contracts, readers, SQL repositories, manifests, projectors, workers, startup probes, lifecycle source, shared browser/desktop client source, static caller/absence searches and isolated fake or disposable tests. |

### Diagnostic, Warning, And Health Contracts

| Contract | Route/reader lineage | Field derivation and failure behavior | Current consumer or ignored fields | Snapshot, repeated work and lifecycle boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Warning | Mounted `API-0009` -> access/current config -> `API-0058` metadata-only `API-0061` -> scope -> reused `API-0060` -> optional repair -> response. | `status` is `blocked`, `failed`, `not-needed`, `ready`, `refreshing` or `stale`; progress is `blocked`, `completed`, `failed`, `processing`, `queued` or `stalled`. Freshness is separately derived as `fresh`, `pending` or `stale`. Repair errors are caught and its mutation result is omitted. | `UIR-0040` gates lists with `serving.readable`; `UIR-0041` uses scope, status/reason/progress, selected counts/rates/times and cleanup. It ignores `serving.usable`, nested manifest/diagnostics, consumer eligibility, aggregate counts, freshness/dirty/runtime/recovery/search detail and many hardcoded zero/null fields. | Retired/LKG is readable/usable because stale is allowed. Two same-key observers per page declare five seconds; deduplication and actual request/mutation count are unobserved. Diagnostic, manifest, scope and optional repair statements are not one snapshot or transaction. |
| Diagnostics | `API-0060` executes one CTE statement over snapshot, selected-import, component-manifest, dirty-work, request, chunk, outbox and reconciliation-cursor state. | Dirty pending includes pending plus stale failed/running; running includes nonstale failed/running; dirty failed is always zero. Chunks are scoped to the preferred latest request; failed request state is suppressed while a claimable chunk exists. Outbox terminal means only `operator_terminal`/`reconciled`. | Warning receives the full object but renders a subset. Health would return direct diagnostics and the reader's manifest diagnostics. No independent HTTP contract owns all fields. | A single statement gives one database statement boundary, not one immutable publication or lifecycle boundary. Mutable inputs can change before scope/manifest/repair reads. Counts do not claim, acknowledge, heartbeat, finalize or clean rows. |
| Reader/manifest | `API-0058` and source-only `API-0059` always obtain diagnostics before active/LKG manifest selection. | Result is `accepted` or `rejected`; manifest freshness is ready/stale/indexing/unavailable. Metadata-only skips serving SQL but not diagnostics/manifest. Missing identity/components, rejected manifest and admission failure remain distinct reasons. | Callers translate or discard reasons differently. Warning exposes derived readability/status; health would nest raw reader status/manifest. | Candidate composition, component state, current manifest lookup, promotion, prior-active retirement and LKG selection are separate. Promotion does not make component manifests immutable. |
| Health | Source-only blocked `API-0017` -> access/config/scope probes -> direct diagnostics in parallel with health reader -> response. | Would return current scope plus direct diagnostics and accepted/rejected manifest state. Errors have no certified mounted HTTP mapping. | No current caller, poller or product field consumer exists. | Direct diagnostics and reader-owned diagnostics repeat the same control-plane work; reachability remains blocked and no lifecycle/status transition is inferred from its registry declaration. |

### Readiness And Polling Ownership

| Caller | Source cadence/key and predicate | Fields consumed or ignored | Failure/recovery boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Runtime route | Public `API-0062`; optional owner probe has a one-second timeout and requires exact runtime version plus `ready:true` and `duckdbOwner:true`. | Returns capabilities, owner/URL/proxy, exposure flags, role, version and `ready`; no durable readiness row or local DuckDB query. | HTTP remains 200 when semantic readiness is false. An unreachable/incompatible owner becomes `ready:false`; the route does not repair the owner. |
| Shared root | `['backend-availability']`, 15 seconds, focus and reconnect enabled. | Consumes only `ready`; ignores role, owner, URL, proxy, capabilities and exposure flags. | Throws/shows Backend unavailable until `ready===true`; manual retry is separate client state. |
| Settings | `['runtime-ready']`, 15 seconds, stale 60 seconds, focus disabled. | Consumes only `settingsDiagnosticsApiExposed`, defaulting a missing value to true; ignores `ready` and every other field. | A truthy exposure flag enables two downstream five-second diagnostics polls plus a runtime-state request. Distinct keys permit repeated readiness work and a waterfall. |
| Desktop main | Fetch every 250 ms for at most 30 seconds. | Consumes only `response.ok`; does not parse `data.ready`. | A 200 `ready:false` ends startup wait, after which the shared root can show unavailable. Timeout is startup failure; exact semantic-ready parity is unproved. |
| Supervisor/dev/operator | Source paths use either transport success or semantic ready/owner/version predicates; adjacent desktop and server-stack locks have separate acquire/heartbeat/reclaim/release lifecycles. | Consumers use different subsets; no single field contract governs all. | Startup retry, process ownership, stale-lock replacement and later renderer state are separate. No actual deployed process or browser/desktop capture ran. |

### Rebuild, Bulk, PDF, Recovery, And Retention Ownership

| Plane | Durable state and observed progress | Mutation, failure and recovery | Retention and unsupported proof |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rebuild request | `DBO-0127` priority/status/admission/retry/lease/error/timestamps and named diagnostics; warning may boost priority or request a bounded rebuild. | Request creation, admission, readmission, finalization and failure are separate repository/worker transitions. Foreground warning mutation is conditional, caught and not returned. | No terminal request cleanup horizon, durable phase fence or deployed request history is proven. |
| Rebuild chunks | `DBO-0128` status, claimability, lease expiry, retry, split, budget, row/byte/prompt/temp estimates/actuals, timings and diagnostics feed `API-0060`. | Worker claim, heartbeat, write, validation, completion, split, request repair/finalization and promotion are separate; status can change with zero projector patch rows. | Diagnostics does not prove chunk output, acknowledgement, immutable snapshot publication or terminal/orphan cleanup. |
| Dirty/component/snapshot | `DBO-0108`, `DBO-0109`, `DBO-0112`, `DBO-0116`, `DBO-0117`, `DBO-0119` bind dirty state, acknowledgement, input watermarks, component identity, selected import and serving manifest. | Intake, claim, component write, acknowledgement, candidate validation, promotion, active/LKG read and startup repair occur at different boundaries. | An in-process lock or mutable manifest does not prove durable claim uniqueness, immutable component identity, replay completion or complete cleanup. |
| Add job | `DBO-0130` keyed `review.bulk.selection`; client consumes status, processed/total, error and local ID every two seconds. | Worker claims the oldest pending/stale row, selects at most 500 IDs, performs add side effects, then separately increments progress by selected IDs. Unknown status polls forever; terminal invalidates list queries. | Selected count is not inserted/existing/conflict result truth. There is no owner-token fence, atomic side-effect/progress write, complete crash replay, job cleanup or retained-history policy. |
| PDF job | Same durable table with `review.pdf.selection`; status reader maps counts/times and fallbacks, including cancelled -> failed. | Per-article file/article/delta effects precede separate job progress. Worker heartbeat surrounds batch execution but not every selection/progress phase. | No client polls the mounted status route. Completion does not prove files, deltas, pin settlement, cleanup, retention or download integrity. |
| Bulk executor | Stale-running reclaim is 15 minutes; heartbeat is five minutes; batch 500; poll two seconds; maximum three attempts with ten-second error backoff. | Cancellation is checked after claim. Side effects and job progress are separate; retries have no persisted claimant token. Source-default desktop `6400MiB` suppresses the only bulk heartbeat. | Executor registration is not execution proof. Restart replay/idempotency, orphan cleanup, terminal retention and browser/desktop progress remain unresolved. |
| Startup probe/recovery | `DBO-0278`, `DBO-0291`, `DBO-0292`, `DBO-0296` track temporary probes, database/WAL and recovery artifacts. | Probe mutation/restore can trigger WAL/index repair; up to three recovery iterations preserve/quarantine/copy/rebuild and a runtime fatal wrapper retries once. | Restoring a chosen row and retaining a recovery manifest do not prove crash-safe startup, data-preserving repair or operator restore validation. |
| Serving retention | `DBO-0132` stores a rotating table cursor; worker considers cleanup every 60 seconds, at most 16 scopes and one 512-row table batch per scope. | Active/LKG/pins protect 11 final tables; rebuild priority can skip a cleanup cycle. | No single-owner lease/full sweep is proven. Requests, chunks, deltas, dirty/ack/control rows, partials, bulk jobs and pins are not covered by this cleanup. |

## US-047 Search, Selection, And Add-To-Project Lineage

US-047 traces submitted search state, materialized title prefixes, dormant
substring work, select-all and selected-ID state, durable job admission,
keyset selection, snapshot ownership, current-table hydration, project writes,
progress, retries, recovery and cleanup at commit
`b4649bd8059a835dcc0d04bfb0d685ebb443d6e7`. UI totals, filter signatures,
job criteria, selected batches, writer outcomes and persisted progress are
kept as separate contracts. A durable job or pin is not treated as frozen
membership, exact insertion truth, terminal cleanup or actual browser/desktop
execution.

### US-047 Evidence Boundary

### Search Mode, Criteria, And Result Ownership

| Operation | Request/criteria and signature | Candidate/result identity and bounds | Snapshot, hydration and lifecycle boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mounted prefix search | Submitted UI text is trimmed and copied into each route query/filter key. Projector tokenizer normalizes NFKD, strips combining marks, lowercases, splits non-ASCII-alphanumeric separators and deduplicates tokens. | Lists/counts and bulk-filter SQL require an `EXISTS` match for every token prefix before route-specific ordering/limit. No standalone token-row result is returned to the UI. | Candidate rows are snapshot serving data. Later add hydration is current-table state and is not frozen by the search snapshot. |
| Standalone prefix contract | Internal `searchReviewServing({searchMode:'tokenPrefix'})` receives text, not a product filter body. | One active-snapshot page, ordered `token,article_id`, max 50 rows / 2 MB / 5 s; the service exposes no caller cursor and passes one whole trimmed lowercase prefix rather than the embedded token set. | Underlying token table has projector/publication/retention lineage, but there is no mounted/browser consumer or runtime result evidence. |
| Async substring contract | Deterministic ID hashes project/config/snapshot/search identity/text/filter signature; pending cursor starts `{cursor:null,limit:500}`. Conflict only refreshes `updated_at`. | One newest job row / 100 KB / 5 s. No persisted membership/result rows, selected-ID manifest or executor exists. Synchronous substring is rejected. | Snapshot ID is stored without a pin; cleanup can retire its serving rows. Job expiry is unset and no progress, terminal, retry, repair or cleanup writer exists. |
| Mapped bulk substring | Registry maps add-by-filter to `review.bulk.substringSelection`, but the mounted route creates `review.bulk.selection` with token-prefix or no-search mode. | One job row / 500 KB / 5 s is a read-result budget, not a route payload cap. Worker throws `waiting for async search results` before candidate selection. | No search-result identity is attached to the bulk job; status retries/failure do not create substring membership. |
| Select-all/add by filter | UI persists a boolean and submits current list mode, status, prompt, duplicate/conflict, date and applied-search fields. Signature canonicalizes filters plus search text; criteria also contains a random request ID. | No route/service byte cap. Initial result is operation metadata; after work it is replaced by last article/batch metadata. No durable selected-ID manifest or displayed-count snapshot exists. | Mounted route is latest/no-pin. Admission observes one active manifest, while every worker batch can select from a newer active snapshot/search identity. |
| Add by explicit IDs | UI sends selected keys; route accepts one string or an array. Criteria preserves raw order/duplicates and `providedTotal` is raw length. | Max 5,000 IDs and 1,000,000 stable-JSON bytes. Worker sorts ascending without `DISTINCT`, max 500. Writer deduplicates each batch; no inserted-ID result manifest exists. | No serving snapshot or pin. IDs hydrate from current article/membership/judgment tables at execution time. |

The contract row/byte/time budgets above govern bounded read results. They do
not cap mounted filter/search request bytes, freeze select-all membership,
bound total multi-batch work, or certify a physical plan.

### Keyset, Write, Progress, Retry, And Cleanup Ownership

| Boundary | Durable/source behavior | Duplicate, failure and recovery behavior | Unsupported authority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Job admission | `app.review_bulk_operation_job` stores kind/project, optional snapshot/pin/config/composed identity, signature, criteria, cursor, batch, status, result, selected progress, retry/error and timestamps. | Pin acquisition and job insertion are separate. `ON CONFLICT(job_id)` resets selected runtime fields but retains several prior identity/criteria fields; route UUIDs normally avoid reuse. | No natural-idempotency contract, request-reuse guarantee, pin/job atomicity or full JSON schema/version exists. |
| Explicit-ID keyset | `json_each`/unnest rows order by article ID, predicate `> cursor` and limit 500; raw total includes duplicates. | Duplicate values are selected and counted. Writer's per-batch `Set` collapses them; if one equal ID fills a batch, the strict next cursor can skip remaining equal rows. Missing/existing IDs also advance selected progress. | Supplied order, duplicate semantics, total meaning, inserted-ID manifest and exact progress authority are unresolved. |
| Filter keyset | Each batch re-resolves active latest snapshot and search identity, applies list/status/queue/posting/date/prompt/all-prefix predicates, `DISTINCT` IDs, `> cursor`, ascending order, max 500. | Newer membership below the cursor is never revisited; removals/additions or identity changes can shift later batches. Pinned generic jobs use stored snapshot but no mounted add route requests one. | “Latest” is not one selection snapshot; count/filter/signature equality and pinned eligibility/retention are unresolved. |
| Current hydration and writes | Writer deduplicates batch IDs, reads current articles, current target membership and current judgments, then transactionally inserts project membership, prompt links and deltas for returned inserts. | `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` makes repeated membership inserts tolerant, but side effect commits before progress. Invalid/existing rows can yield zero inserts while the job advances. | Current-versus-snapshot field policy, all side-effect idempotency, write-result persistence and exactly-once progress are unresolved. |
| Cursor/result/progress | Cursor starts `{cursor:null,jobId,limit}`. Progress update stores last ID/size and increments `processed_count` by selected batch size; exact-full final batches need a later empty selection to complete. | Initial operation metadata is replaced. Writer totals are ignored. A crash after write and before progress can replay the same selection; stale reclaim can overlap an old claimant. | Processed/total/result do not prove membership inserts, ordering completeness or a single claimant. |
| Retry and recovery | Claim order is oldest `updated_at,job_id` among pending or 15-minute-stale running. Five-minute heartbeat surrounds batch execution. Initial attempt plus three retries are possible; cancel is checked after claim. | No owner-token/CAS fence guards later heartbeat/progress/terminal updates. Handled batch failures can immediately return to the loop; persistent jobs rely on a later executor for stale recovery. | Restart completion, retry backoff authority, concurrent claimant exclusion and configured desktop execution remain unresolved. |
| Pins and cleanup | Pinned generic jobs acquire/refcount deterministic pins, default 24 hours. Active positive-ref, future-expiry pins protect final serving/base rows. Mounted add flows are latest/no-pin. | Release/expire functions exist but have no non-test caller. Expiry eventually stops retention protection without deleting the row. Job/search `expires_at` remains null and no terminal job/result/pin deletion path was found. | Pin settlement, orphan repair, terminal history, retention horizon, complete cleanup and physical deletion are unresolved. |

## US-048 PDF, Export, And Transfer Lineage

US-048 ties generated outputs and portability mappings to their separate
selection, hydration, serialization, file, download, cleanup and recovery
owners at commit `39dd13be9001480df830311dcf7578ba307e35b4`.
A durable selected-ID result does not freeze later CSV hydration, a transfer
database transaction does not freeze asset copies performed afterward, and a
ready status/checksum does not prove that a client verified or retained the
downloaded bytes. Static transfer limit constants, execution-mode thresholds
and enforced resource gates are also kept as separate contracts.

### US-048 Evidence Boundary

### Output Contracts And Ownership Boundaries

| Output | Criteria, job/pin and selected result | Hydration, serialization and file | Cleanup, recovery and unsupported boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PDF fetch | Filter/project requests store review config, filters/search, force/concurrency and random request identity with latest/no-pin semantics; explicit IDs are no-snapshot and capped. `DBO-0130` holds cursor, selected progress and cumulative PDF counters, not a file manifest. | Worker selects ascending IDs in pages up to 500, deduplicates before current article load, skips existing/user-uploaded PDFs unless forced, then tries original URL, Unpaywall and arXiv. File write, article fields and review delta are not one transaction. | Initial attempt plus three worker retries; five-minute heartbeat has no claimant token. No job/pin/file orphan retention path. UI only displays creation ID; later file link is a separate rooted runtime-asset read. |
| Project review CSV | `review.export.selection` stores metadata/prompt/source criteria, latest or pinned semantics, cursor and a dynamic `batches.<lastArticleId>` selected-ID map. Generic explicit-ID caps apply; declared 10 MB output budget does not. Optional generic pins are acquired separately and have no terminal release caller. | Completed download reconstructs ID batches, re-resolves source scopes, hydrates snapshot serving payload/detail plus current article/authors/raw payload, then streams selected columns. No server CSV is written. | Selection does not freeze all hydrated fields. No aggregate byte cap, checksum, receipt, result/pin cleanup or download recovery. Browser/desktop/OS owns `<project>_export_<date>.csv`. |
| Prompt CSV | Selected prompt IDs go directly to current `app.prompt`; no job, pin, selected-ID manifest or snapshot. | Fixed Prompt Heading/Answer Options/Prompt columns become a response Blob and client-saved dated file. | No route-level aggregate cap, checksum, durable receipt, retry/cleanup ownership or actual browser/desktop save proof. |
| Transfer export | Summary/preflight are current reads, not a pin. Export has no review-serving job or result manifest. Current database rows are serialized in one transaction; inline output has no session, while background work creates an export session/result payload. | Deterministically ordered payloads, later asset copies and manifest become a v2 ZIP. Ready metadata stores package bytes/SHA-256/logical fingerprint/filename/expiry; background package stays under `tmp/project-transfer/export/<id>`. | Database and assets have different capture times. Stale work is failed/cleaned, ready bytes expire, and terminal rows prune later. No download lease/client integrity check/retained-copy policy or actual runtime proof. |
| Transfer read/import | Import session and upload checksum own the archive. Analyze produces revisioned analysis/manifest/plan/payload artifacts, target mappings and dirty-token snapshot; there is no snapshot pin. Plan revision, staging revision and target-state tokens fence commit admission. | ZIP/manifest/payload checks feed source-to-target project/article/prompt/route/model/provider/judgment/history ID maps. Assets promote before one database transaction writes target rows, deltas, history and dirty tokens. | History can recover committed completion; otherwise stale work fails and owned temp/promoted files clean. Successful asset retention, malformed-manifest recovery completeness, plan delivery to normal UI and deployed restore/runtime proof remain unresolved. |

### Threshold, Gate, Progress, And Recovery Truth

| Contract | Enforced source behavior | Not established |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Execution thresholds | Export inline only at package <=128 MiB and assets <=64 MiB; analyze inline only with supplied expanded <=512 MiB and ZIP <=128 MiB; commit backgrounds at article >=25,000, judgment >=250,000, combined >=50,000 or assets >=2 GiB. Missing expanded bytes make the normal UI analyze request background. | Thresholds route execution; they are not accepted-package/output caps or a physical memory guarantee. Preflight can drift from actual build. |
| Resource gates | Safe temp/archive/runtime paths, nonnegative counters and available disk >= target bytes plus 10% are enforced at call sites. ZIP structure, CRC, size and compression checks are separate. | Named 100,000-member/inode, 100x ratio, 16 GiB expanded, depth 64, 1,000,000 JSON members, 16 MiB line and 2 GiB file constants are not compared by `validateProjectTransferResourceGates`; the focused test deliberately accepts values above them. |
| Export progress | Queued -> assembling -> packaging -> ready; 60-second heartbeat; row/byte/phase/warning fields persist and mirror to progress file/runtime log. Actual background crossing can persist an already-built ready package. | Progress does not prove source snapshot, file completeness, client receipt or cleanup-safe concurrent download. Stale work fails rather than resumes. |
| Import progress | Upload -> queued -> extracting/analyzing -> awaiting resolution/ready -> committing -> completed, with owner leases, plan/staging revisions, byte/row/item counts, warnings and performance metrics. Analyze/commit heartbeat every 15 seconds. | UI sees only returned fields; normal reads omit the plan. Completion progress/session/artifact cleanup is best-effort after the database transaction. |
| Recovery | Active writer scans 50 by default/max 500; export queued stale at 10 minutes, export/analyze/commit owner stale at five minutes. Analysis can recover coherent artifacts; import history repairs committed sessions. Terminal cleanup marker precedes 24-hour-later eligible row pruning. | No export resume, download lease, successful promoted-asset cleanup, malformed-manifest guarantee, deployed interruption run or operator restore validation. |

## US-049 Article, Import, And Project-Scope Mutation Lineage

US-049 traces source mutations forward at commit
`744a6122fbcfca972b6df6423eab66dee13448bc`. It keeps data-source
configuration, import-route definition, canonical article state, current and
historical import links, project-route membership, direct membership, durable
deltas, dirty intake, physical scope, selected import, serving publication,
files and cleanup as separate contracts. In particular, durable reconciliation
is not publication: both intake services can mark a source delta reconciled
after deriving zero dirty work from current scope or route membership.

### US-049 Evidence Boundary

| Boundary | Recorded result |
| --- | --- |
| Source identity | Commit `744a6122fbcfca972b6df6423eab66dee13448bc`; Ralph's pre-existing `tasks/prd.json` timestamp-only modification remains untouched. |
| Prerequisite | US-048 is complete. US-032 mutation inventory, US-035-US-038 projector/lifecycle results, US-039 portability, US-045 payload lineage and US-048 export/transfer lineage remain authoritative and are refined rather than replaced. |
| Allowed evidence | Exact route/service/projector/worker code, serializers, SQL builders, migrations already inventoried, static caller/absence searches, schema/manifests, file paths and isolated fake/disposable tests. |
| Prohibited evidence | No live/current DuckDB, configured snapshot/query/studio, product server/app/browser/desktop shell, production import, worker, projector, cleanup, repair, export/transfer, migration, benchmark or physical profile ran. |
| State and disposition | Fifteen new `LIN-####` rows use only US-001 `auditStatus`. `proofCheckState`, `recommendationActionability`, `overallCertification`, every definition and every storage disposition remain independent and unchanged. Unsupported homes and disposition decisions remain unresolved. |

### Source Mutation And Invalidation Contracts

| Mutation family | Source write and retained fields | Delta/invalidation | Explicit non-equivalence or gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Data source and route catalog | `app.data_source` retains title/description/route/cursor/date/archive timestamps; `app.import_route` is a separate active route identity. The declared `app.data_source_import_route` bridge has no production owner. | No data-source delta exists. Import-store route ensure/upsert does not itself select projects. | Archiving a source does not deactivate a route, remove current links, change project-route membership, enqueue review work, delete source files or create a recovery journal. |
| Canonical article | Matcher creates/reuses `app.article`; import resolver can change authors, created time, summary, title, identifiers, publication status, source metadata and URL. Full-text/PDF writers own additional fields. | Changed canonical fields map independently to display, search and judgment-input deltas; one source write can append zero to three review delta rows. | Raw/original/import data and every physical article column are not one delta vocabulary. Reference-based update suppression and identifier races mean import acceptance is not canonical replacement proof. |
| Current import link and source history | Current `app.article_import_route`, historical/quarantinable source record, strong identifiers/quarantine, raw/import/match JSON and typed hot facts write under distinct keys. | New current link emits add; source-key/hash or typed rank/filter change emits rank; stale sync emits remove/rank tombstone. | Source-record history is not selected-current truth; hot fact is not raw JSON; a tombstoned link is not a deleted canonical article. Only Covidence currently invokes complete stale sync. |
| Project route membership | Create/edit/clone/transfer write `app.project_import_route`; edit replaces the set when allowed. | One `project.reviewConfig.updated` row with `importRoutes` requests broad rebuild. Existing import deltas previously reconciled without that project are not replayed by route selection. | Project-route link, physical scope, component manifest and selected-import winner are four different records and publication instants. |
| Direct project membership | Add/clone/subproject/transfer write `app.project_article`; direct delete removes it. | Add/remove scope deltas affect nine components; direct delete emits removal only when no route still supplies scope. | `RETURNING` ties normal add deltas to inserted rows; subproject conflict-ignore does not. A scope delta is not physical membership and can be acknowledged without a scope-table write. |
| Project/data-source archive and hard delete | Project archive/unarchive flips `app.project.archived`; delete request/cleanup progresses through `app.archived_project_delete_tombstone`. Data-source delete is soft archive. | Project archive/unarchive emits config rebuild; data-source archive and hard cleanup emit no article/import/scope delta. | Reversible archive, delete admission, bounded hard cleanup, current V4 invalidation, file deletion, source-history retention and operator recovery are separate contracts. |

### Delta, Dirty Work, And Replay Matrix

| Boundary | Durable identity and ordering | Acknowledgement/publication | Replay, repair and retained-state boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Article delta | Table/row/partition/operation, typed key, mutation-key hash, separately allocated high water, payload version and optional project/content flags | Direct source transaction appends display/search/judgment-input rows; later intake orders by high water and delta ID. | Duplicate identity returns the existing delta. No operating outbox backs current writers, and direct metadata backfills bypass the delta path. |
| Import delta | Route/article/source-record key/hash, rank/year, tombstone, payload and high water | Add/remove/rank rows join typed hot facts and current selected projects before component dirty upsert. | Replayed identical append is idempotent, but intake-time null project is terminally reconciled with no late-route replay. Delta/hot/source rows have no cleanup registry or approved retention horizon. |
| Review intake | Payload JSON is parsed/spread, then typed columns and field sets overlay it; article-only rows fan out through current physical scope. | One bounded transaction upserts component/project dirty identity and stamps every fetched delta `reconciled_at`. | Zero current scope means zero dirty rows plus reconciliation. There is no immutable fan-out snapshot, separate intake checkpoint or repair that discovers later scope. |
| Import intake | Current hot facts and current project-route links supply dirty projects and rank fields. | One bounded transaction writes dirty components and stamps all fetched import deltas reconciled. | Missing typed facts fail the batch; valid null-project rows do not. Later route selection/config rebuild is distinct and does not replay the original delta. |
| Dirty claim and component write | Dirty identity is component/project with range/watermark, not source-row identity; claims and projection manifests are separate. | Generic writer can transact physical component writes, manifest/watermark and acknowledgement; project-scope incremental writes no physical rows. | Status plus timestamps are not a durable owner fence; no complete acknowledged-dirty compaction/history/retention contract exists. Full rebuild repair is separately admitted/chunked. |

### Projector, Manifest, And Serving Publication

| Component | Current input and physical output | Manifest/publication boundary | Mutation-specific blocker retained |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Project scope | Current project route/direct links, current article and project archived/date fields -> `mart.project_scope_article` only in rebuild chunks | Incremental path advances projection manifest, acknowledgement and watermark with no scope mutation; chunk count/checksum and snapshot promotion are later steps. | Acknowledged add/remove/config work can coexist with stale physical scope until a full rebuild; concurrent route/date/archive changes are not frozen to the chunk identity. |
| Selected import | Physical scope + current project routes + non-tombstone hot facts/current link -> `app.review_selected_article_import_v4`; range refresh can write final serving | Full cursor/header completion and component manifest are separate. Dirty path rewrites the selected base beneath a completed header and directly changes final serving. | Winner ordering is typed-fact code, not raw-payload authority. Completed snapshot mutability, base/final atomicity, no-op patch budget/reset and concurrent cleanup remain unresolved. |
| Display and payload | Physical scope + canonical article + selected base/current source -> `mart.review_article_serving_v4` and `mart.review_article_serving_payload_v4` | Display base, direct display patch and payload replacement have distinct writes/counts/manifests; status components later update final rows. | Canonical/import metadata merge, Covidence URL fallback, previews and byte estimates can reflect different source instants; final serving is not one atomic component transaction. |
| Search, status and queue | Scope/selected/canonical plus judgments/config -> title tokens and direct final status/queue rows | Search can be optional/indexing; LLM/Human status and queue publish under separate identities and acknowledgements. | Import/scope invalidation registry membership does not prove exact row change, tokenizer parity, queue grain, or simultaneous reader visibility. |
| Posting, counts, facets and options | Scope/selected/final/detail/queue inputs -> posting/stats and summary outputs | Incremental/direct publication and request-wide chunk reduction/finalization are separate; finalizer can refresh stats/options and then promote. | Successful component chunks do not make derived outputs one transaction or prove partial cleanup, count/facet parity, or same-snapshot visibility. |
| Manifest/promotion/retention | Mutable component manifests compose candidate snapshot; promotion records active/LKG; pins affect retention | Retention rotates one 512-row delete batch among eleven final/base tables per scope. | Source tables, deltas, hot facts, physical scope, manifests/requests/chunks/partials and import files are outside that eleven-table registry; archived cleanup is a different incomplete registry. |

## US-050 Judgment And Human-Review Mutation Lineage

US-050 traces review-decision mutations forward at commit
`fcadc01a49da01848c5deaca853a4516f664d0a2`. It keeps active LLM natural
identity, physical delete generation, job-local completion, canonical import,
per-project invalidation, Human pending state, answer state, old/new prompt
identity, overlays, comparison invalidation, component publication and cleanup
as separate contracts. A source mutation is therefore not considered visible
merely because its delta reconciled or one component acknowledged it.

### US-050 Evidence Boundary

| Boundary | Recorded result |
| --- | --- |
| Source identity | Commit `fcadc01a49da01848c5deaca853a4516f664d0a2`; Ralph's pre-existing `tasks/prd.json` timestamp-only modification remains untouched. |
| Prerequisite | US-049 is complete. US-033 mutation inventory, US-035-US-038 projector/lifecycle results, US-043 queue lineage and US-049 delta/intake lineage remain authoritative and are refined rather than replaced. |
| Allowed evidence | Exact route/service/projector/worker code, serializers, SQL builders, migrations already inventoried, static caller/absence searches, manifests and isolated fake/disposable tests. |
| Prohibited evidence | No live/current DuckDB, configured snapshot/query/studio, product server/app/browser/desktop shell, production judgment job, projector, rebuild, repair, cleanup, migration, benchmark or physical profile ran. |
| State and disposition | Fifteen new `LIN-####` rows and two promoted prior lineage rows use only US-001 `auditStatus`. `proofCheckState`, `recommendationActionability`, `overallCertification`, every definition and every storage disposition remain independent and unchanged. Unsupported homes remain unresolved. |
