### Model, Content, And Mutation Identity Contracts

| Contract | Exact dimensions | Current behavior | Non-equivalence retained |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Active LLM natural identity | Article, prompt, model, `use_title`, `use_abstract`, `use_fulltext`, `use_fulltext_no_images`, with `deleted_at IS NULL` | Completion treats an existing active row as immutable; legacy direct writer updates it. | Physical uniqueness adds `delete_generation`; a deleted generation-zero row can still occupy the key. |
| Execution snapshot | Job, queue, claim, article, prompt, model, four content flags, payload hash/JSON | Claim-time settings validate completion and local outbox payload. | Snapshot identity is not the canonical judgment key, current project config, review hash or comparison identity. |
| LLM delta identity | Explicit project/article/prompt/model/four flags/judgment plus source partition/high water | Import fans one canonical row to currently visible projects; other writers choose different project sets. | Current visibility, stored nullable `project_id`, project scope and comparison projects are not one fan-out authority. |
| Current projection configuration | Project model/provider execution identity, four flags, Human mode and enabled prompts | Full/status/queue/detail/summary paths re-read different current inputs under component/snapshot context. | A source delta does not freeze later current-table joins or make component visibility atomic. |
| Human natural identities | Prompt mode `(project,article,prompt)`; summary mode `(project,article)`; row ID is the delta/overlay Human key | Pending, answered, imported, moved and summary rows share only part of this identity. | `is_answered`, nonblank `answer`, Covidence origin, queue eligibility and UI completion are separate predicates. |

### LLM And Human Mutation Matrix

| Operation family | Source mutation | Delta, dirty and comparison behavior | RYW, replay, cleanup and gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Current LLM create | Owner or judge-worker completion persists job-local outbox and queue/ack state; canonical import later uses generation zero. | Import emits `judgment.llm.created` per currently visible project, directly intakes dirty work, and invalidates comparisons only for newly inserted canonical rows. | Marker-idempotent replay exists; local acknowledgement/prune is postcommit. Duplicate canonical rows can still receive created deltas while comparison invalidation is inserted-only. |
| Legacy LLM create/update | Callable writer inserts or mutates one active seven-dimension row. | Per-visible-project created/updated deltas and comparison stale writes share the transaction. | No non-test caller, outbox or durable retry; the outer catch logs and resolves. No normal-list overlay. |
| LLM delete | Project cleanup soft-deletes and bumps generation; invalid/admin paths do not bump; merge can hard-delete collisions. | Project cleanup emits edited-project delete; invalid uses stored nullable project; admin emits none; merge fan-out is broad; comparison invalidation is inconsistent. | No shared replay/repair. Deleted-at-only generation zero can block equivalent recreate; broad config work is not an exact row tombstone. |
| LLM move | Prompt merge changes noncolliding `prompt_id`; collisions are deleted. | Collision deletes emit selected project tombstones; noncollision moves emit no old/new row delta. | Later broad prompt/config work cannot prove exact old-key removal/new-key creation or comparison convergence. |
| Human pending create/delete | Init/drift inserts missing unanswered rows and deletes drifted unanswered rows. | No Human delta, dirty row, overlay or comparison invalidation. | One transaction per article but no reviewer claim, replay, expiry, retention or cleanup owner. |
| Human answer/update | Submit updates answer/comment and sets `is_answered=true`. | Nonblank rows emit Human-updated delta plus overlay; blank optional rows emit neither. All selected rows separately invalidate comparison. | Client refetches init only. Overlay has no product reader/reconciler/sweeper; async serving components remain the normal visibility path. |
| Human import/create/clear | Covidence, clone and transfer upsert prompt/summary rows; clear deletes them. | All use Human-updated when they emit; delete operation supplies tombstone. Clone/transfer behavior and comparison invalidation differ. | No common idempotency/replay/retention contract; imports generally create no immediate overlay. |
| Human move/delete | Project cleanup hard-deletes; prompt merge deletes collisions or moves answered/nonblank rows to the keep prompt. | Project delete/collision delete have no Human tombstone; move emits only the new prompt update and no old-key delta. | Broad prompt/config rebuild does not establish row-level removal, old/new ordering or RYW. |
| Legacy review/assessment | Transfer inserts/reuses review and assessment rows; merge moves/deletes assessments; archived cleanup deletes families. | No review/assessment-specific review delta, overlay or comparison invalidation. | Ordinary ownership, recovery, retention and intended serving effect remain unresolved. |

### Delta, Dirty Work, And Component Publication

| Boundary | Durable behavior | Exact downstream effect | Missing or non-atomic boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Delta ledger | Deterministic idempotency hashes source mutation key, operation, partition, row, table and typed key; high water allocates separately. | Delete operation or deleted/removed kind supplies tombstone; payload and typed columns persist together without SQL coherence checks. | Idempotency cannot repair an omitted event, wrong project fan-out, old-key absence or broad change kind. |
| Invalidation registry | LLM created/updated/deleted -> LLM status, queue, payload, posting, summary; Human updated -> Human status plus the same four downstream families. | Status is first; every affected component receives its own projection dirty identity. | Human has no created/deleted/moved vocabulary. Registry order is not a cross-component transaction or visibility fence. |
| Review intake | Payload is parsed, typed columns overlay it, required keys are checked, and explicit-project judgment rows do not scope-fan-out. | One transaction upserts all component dirty rows and stamps the delta reconciled. | Missing/nullable project or malformed typed identity blocks the ordered batch; reconciliation does not mean any serving row published. |
| Dirty claim/ack | Deterministic component/project dirty rows coalesce high waters; stale running/failed work is reclaimable after 15 minutes. | Completion inserts acknowledgement and can advance component watermark in the writer transaction. | Status/timestamp has no durable owner token or fence; acknowledgement compaction has no production caller. |
| Status | LLM/Human projectors aggregate current/delta state and directly update final candidate/active serving rows. | Status/count fields, manifest, ack and watermark can share the component transaction. | Returned patch count can be zero despite physical mutation; LLM and Human status are distinct publications. |
| Queue/detail | Queue deletes/reinserts current pairs; detail independently rebuilds current LLM/Human payload rows. | Each writes under its own component/snapshot identity with later readers and retention. | Queue formulas differ from status and pending semantics; detail rehydration is not overlay or source-snapshot fixedness. |
| Posting/summary/options | Posting diff/stats and summary count/facet outputs read current serving/detail/queue state. | Incremental summary commits before option refresh; full partial reduction/finalization refreshes derived outputs before promotion. | Contributions, partial rows, accumulators, final tables and options have separate cleanup and failure/replay boundaries. |
| Snapshot publication | Generic writer is atomic only for one supplied component operation. Candidate validation/composition and promotion are separate. | Active/LKG readers and snapshot-protected retention consume published identities. | Component success does not freeze mutable manifests or prove simultaneous status/queue/detail/summary visibility. |

### Read-Your-Write, Replay, Repair, And Retention

| Concern | Supported path | Unsupported boundary retained |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LLM RYW | Job-local state can show completion before canonical import; no review-list/detail overlay exists. | A completed local job is not immediate canonical or serving visibility. |
| Human RYW | Submit response reports only updated count; client refetches Human init. A nonblank row overlay is written with a default five-minute TTL. | Product readers do not consume the overlay, and no production reconciliation/expiry/delete path exists. Blank submissions have no overlay or delta. |
| Source replay | Local LLM marker/outbox replay is durable across the DuckDB commit/local ack boundary. Delta append itself is idempotent. | Legacy LLM, Human submit/import/move/delete and admin cleanup have no shared durable mutation journal; omitted deltas cannot be reconstructed from acknowledgement alone. |
| Projection repair | Dirty reclaim, request/chunk repair, full rebuild admission and snapshot promotion paths exist. | Claims lack durable fencing; component repair does not recreate missing source events or comparison invalidation and does not make publication one transaction. |
| Restart recovery | Judging owner/judge-worker startup replays journals, repairs leases and flushes outbox; review worker can recover request/chunk state. | Ready local runtime rows may be discarded/rebuilt rather than resumed; direct/Human transactions and split prompt merge have different or absent recovery. |
| Retention/cleanup | Local outbox visibility prune, checkpoint/file deletion and protected final-table retention have source-defined owners. | Source judgments/Human rows, deltas, dirty/ack/watermark/manifests, overlays, pending rows, contribution/partial state and comparison invalidation are outside one complete retained-state registry. |

## US-051 Project Review-Configuration Forward Lineage

US-051 traces the configuration writers frozen by US-034 forward at commit
`50fdbcc5b2a7bf33263f5750f27546bc4f2a1365`. It treats source applicability,
review hash, active judgment identity, dirty identity, mutable component
manifest, selected-import identity, serving snapshot, claim-time execution
snapshot, comparison state and transfer dirty tokens as separate contracts.
An accepted delta, completed dirty item or admitted rebuild is therefore not
treated as proof that a route can read a current-hash published snapshot.

### Configuration And Publication Identities

| Contract | Exact source-observed dimensions | Mutation/publication consequence | Non-equivalence retained |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Source applicability | Project archive, inclusive date bounds, selected route set, current article-route links and direct project/article membership | Writers emit broad project config or per-article scope changes; physical project scope is rebuilt from current tables. | Applicability is not the review hash, a frozen derived membership set or the selected-import ID. |
| Review config hash | Human mode, model ID, provider connection/kind/base, remote model ID, variant, `metadata_json.$.options`, four content flags and sorted active prompt ID/config hash/order | Hash-changing routes require a published active/LKG snapshot under the new value. | Dates, routes, archive, criteria, provider auth/config/secret/enabled/max-inflight and model display/enabled/version are outside it. |
| Active LLM identity | Article, prompt, model and four content flags with `deleted_at IS NULL`; physical key also has `delete_generation` | Current judgments can be reused/projected under matching dimensions. | Provider execution identity, review hash, job snapshot and comparison identity are broader or differently scoped. |
| Dirty projection identity | Projection component plus nullable project ID | Every config delta coalesces into stable component/project dirty rows across later config changes. | Prompt scope, changed fields, review hash, generation and source mutation are not identity dimensions. |
| Component manifest | Component/project projection identity plus mutable definition, config hash, generation, digests and watermarks | Claim preparation reuses the same key and updates its current review hash. | A referenced manifest is not immutable merely because an older snapshot copied its state. |
| Selected-import snapshot | Project, static project-scope projection identity, selected-import definition and import-run-article high water | Full/range projectors write the durable selected base used by serving snapshots. | Review-change high water, date/route state and review hash are absent, so config rebuilds can reuse and rewrite the same selected ID. |
| Serving snapshot | Project, review hash, selected-import ID, source watermarks and copied component states | Candidate validation and promotion expose an active/LKG read identity. | Source tables, current hydration, mutable component manifests and old active hashes are not frozen or retired together. |
| Execution snapshot | Job, queue, claim, article, prompt plus current project/model/provider/content/date/payload fields | Claim-time immutable payload validates completion and later audit. | Job-local SQLite configuration, current review hash and canonical judgment identity remain distinct. |
| Comparison state | Comparison project/generation/stale state with judgment/content/source overlap or explicit project-prompt edit fan-out | Writer-specific calls request comparison rebuild. | Review-serving component rebuild is not comparison invalidation. |
| Transfer target state | Coverage version, per-surface dirty tokens, global unknown token, fingerprints, plan/revision/history | Analysis/commit can detect covered target changes and transfer writes advance broad surfaces. | Ordinary project/prompt/scope config deltas do not advance these tokens. |

### Configuration Mutation-To-Invalidation Matrix

| Mutation family | Source change and benchmark dimensions | Delta, dirty scope and overlays | Later publication, replay and unresolved boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Project core/content/date/archive | Model, four flags, Human mode, dates and archive use `project.reviewConfig.updated`; model/content/mode can change the review hash while dates/archive do not. Protected edits are rejected after a job exists. | Ten project-scoped dirty items: project scope, selected import, judgment input, LLM/Human status, queue, posting, search, summary and payload. No display dirty item, overlay, comparison call or transfer token. | Current config is re-read per component. Direct ledger append shares the route transaction, but no config version/CAS/replay journal or cross-component publication fence exists. |

### Dirty Work, Rebuild, Snapshot, And Route Publication

| Boundary | Durable behavior | Exact downstream effect | Gap preserved |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Delta append | Fields are sorted/deduped and persisted with typed payload, project/prompt key, mutation identity and high water. | Ordinary config writers generally append in the same DuckDB transaction as source rows. | Direct append cannot replay an omitted writer, reconstruct old/new values or prove eventual route publication; ordinary config has no production source-outbox path. |
| Intake/reconciliation | Typed payload is validated, then one stable component/project dirty row is upserted per registry component and the source delta is reconciled. | Project, prompt and direct-scope plans preserve their ten/six/nine component sets. | Reconciled means accepted into current dirty work, not physically projected; stable identity can coalesce multiple config hashes/field sets. |
| Narrow versus broad execution | Prompt work starts at LLM status and remains prompt-scoped where runners support it. Project config starts at project scope; broad project search is converted to a search rebuild and its dirty row completes on admitted work. | Components claim and acknowledge independently; each claim preparation reads the current review hash into its manifest. | Update-mode labels do not prove physical scope, selected base, a candidate, cross-component order or comparison/transfer invalidation. |
| Missing-snapshot repair | A runner that cannot find current candidate/active state requests `missingReviewServingSnapshot` and releases its claims after successful admission. | Fresh bootstrap unions all default components and seeds manifests, deterministic selected/snapshot IDs and a candidate. | Freshness is based on any queued/active project snapshot, not the requested current hash. |
| Existing old active hash | Rebuild stats count active/candidate manifests without a review-hash predicate. With an old active snapshot, missing-current-hash work is a normal rebuild; default chunks expand existing active/candidate component state. | Chunks can rebuild existing state; request finalization refreshes/promotes only candidate targets discovered for the request. | The normal path does not seed a current-hash candidate. An admitted repair can therefore leave current-hash routes without active/LKG state; no exact regression test closes this path. |
| Physical scope and selected base | Project-scope rebuild chunks delete/insert membership by current direct/route/date state. Selected import then deletes/recreates a full root or writes article ranges under its deterministic ID. | Selected base can refresh final serving fields and feed later components. | Incremental scope is control-only; selected ID excludes config/date/route/review-change identity and can be rewritten while old/new serving snapshots reference it. |
| Candidate validation/promotion | Candidate composition copies current component state; validation checks selected completion, component status/hash/watermarks/state. Promotion retires same-hash active state and activates candidate with LKG. | Current-hash list/count/filter/search/job readers can resolve the promoted manifest. | Promotion does not retire old-hash active manifests, freeze later current joins or make derived-output finalization one transaction. |
| Route lookup | LLM/Human/Both/Unassessed and queue/bulk readers compute the current hash and query active then retired/LKG state for that same hash; cursor/SQL predicates bind the hash/snapshot. | Hash-changing config becomes unavailable until matching publication. Hash-neutral config can continue reading the previous same-hash snapshot while rebuild work is pending. | Same-hash availability is not freshness, and an old-hash active snapshot is neither a valid fallback nor evidence that missing-hash recovery succeeded. |

### Execution, Comparison, Transfer, Replay, And Cleanup

| Concern | Source-defined contract | Missing or duplicated deterministic state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Job admission/edit gate | Once any judgment job exists, ordinary edits reject model, four flags, Human mode, dates and routes; prompts require pause/drain rules. | Provider/model repositories can still mutate execution identity. Job-local rows, current project/model/provider, claim snapshot and review hash can disagree without a single version authority. |
| Claim execution snapshot | Claim hydration persists immutable job/queue/claim payload with current content, prompt, project dates, model options and provider config/secret references. | It is not the review-serving snapshot, active judgment key, transfer fingerprint or the initial SQLite job configuration. |
| Comparison | Judgment/Human services derive affected comparison projects; full project-prompt edit explicitly marks source/summary comparisons stale. | Core/content/date/route/mode, provider/model, global prompt, clone, specialized and transfer config do not share that call. Full review rebuild does not prove comparison convergence. |
| Transfer revalidation | Covered dirty-token snapshots and fingerprints can invalidate a materialized transfer plan; provider/model and commit/history writers advance different surface sets. | Ordinary project/prompt/scope/clone/Covidence mutations do not advance tokens, while transfer dependency creation bypasses ordinary project config fan-out. |
| Config replay/repair | Route transactions roll back their direct delta; dirty claims can release/fail/reclaim; rebuild requests/chunks recover and diagnostics can request missing work. Transfer has plan/history recovery. | No durable config mutation journal/version reconstructs omitted/global prompt events, comparison state, old/new values or a missing current-hash candidate. Repair-on-read begins after observed diagnostics and can itself mutate request state. |
| Retention | Eleven serving/base tables delete bounded unprotected rows. Active/LKG/pinned identities protect rows; selected base protection follows active/LKG/pin references. | Every old-hash active manifest remains protected because promotion retires only same-hash active state. Delta, dirty/ack/watermark, component/snapshot manifests, rebuild controls, execution snapshots, overlays and legacy review state lack one complete config-retention registry. |
| Project cleanup | Archive emits broad config and drains jobs; hard cleanup later removes enumerated legacy/project families. | Hard cleanup emits no review delta, omits current V4/control/source families and files, and has no end-to-end restore/deletion receipt. Human-mode/review-state rows have no migration or common cleanup owner. |

## US-052 Publication And Rebuild Lifecycle Trace

US-052 traces the publication and rebuild control rows frozen by US-009,
US-010, US-035-US-038 and US-051 at commit
`03e64e2d4288e1f1ea4ef6747071e93e06c761e3`. Identity, mutable component
state, selected-import state, serving snapshots, rebuild requests, chunks,
partials, acknowledgements, watermarks and pins remain separate contracts. A
completed chunk or failed request is therefore not treated as publication,
retry, retirement, compaction or safe deletion proof.

### Durable Identity And State Separation

| Durable family | Identity and mutable state | Lifecycle traced | Contract that remains separate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dirty work and acknowledgement | Stable dirty ID over component/project/scope; point/range ack over component identity, partition and high water | Upsert/coalesce, claim, release, fail, complete, ack, watermark and dormant compaction | Claim owner/version, attempt history, range authority, terminal retention and deletion |
| Projector watermark | Deterministic application ID plus projector/project/route/component/partition; physical table has no uniqueness fence | Insert/update, source-barrier advance, startup dedupe/probe and read-after-write validation | Cross-process uniqueness, dormant lease/cursor/error state and retention |
| Projection manifest | Stable project/component/projection-identity key with mutable config, definition, generation and watermarks | Create/update, candidate/active use, validation reads and diagnostics | Immutable publication version, status owner, retirement/history and snapshot pin identity |
| Selected-import header/base | Deterministic selected ID plus project/scope; mutable cursor/status and physical article base | Candidate/header update, full reset, range rebuild, completion, validation, retention and startup probe | Owner/lease/failure/retry, immutable membership, concurrent rewrite and header/base orphan cleanup |
| Serving snapshot | Project/snapshot key plus status, review hash, copied component/composed state, selected and LKG references | Candidate create/refresh, validate, activate, same-hash retire, LKG read and failed/startup paths | Single-active constraint, immutable component copies, failed transition owner and cross-hash retirement |
| Snapshot pin | Deterministic identity over project/snapshot/composed state/owner; refcount, expiry and release time | Acquire/increment/release/expire helpers and active/LKG/pin protection | Production settlement, manifest equality/FK, expiry sweep and pin-row cleanup |
| Rebuild request | Deterministic request ID over project/reason/components/watermarks/identity; separate status/admission/retry/lease fields | Create/admit/block, priority, supersede, repair/adopt, readmit, complete/fail and startup repair | Immutable conflict semantics, actual request claim lease, terminal history, retention and deletion |
| Rebuild chunk | Deterministic component/range/input/output identity, optionally request-scoped; status/lease/retry/output metrics | Upsert, claim/heartbeat, build/validate, complete/fail/retry/split/release and stale reclaim | Request/parent/snapshot FKs, idempotent-output crash fence, terminal/orphan retention and delete |
| Summary partials | Request/chunk/project/hash/snapshot/serving or article/contribution keys | Chunk replace, completed-chunk reduction, accumulator refresh, source-partial delete and final serving write | Atomic reduction receipt, contribution/accumulator cleanup, failed/superseded ownership and retention |
| Final serving/base rows | Project/hash/snapshot/component-specific physical identities | Component replace/patch, request finalization, active/LKG/pin protection and bounded deletion | Request/chunk status, manifest mutability, current-table hydration and complete storage lifecycle |

### Required Lifecycle Verb Trace

| Lifecycle verb | Exact durable behavior | Failure/restart boundary retained |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create | Intake creates/coalesces dirty rows; projectors create mutable manifests/selected headers; fresh bootstrap creates candidate/request/chunks; chunked summary creates partials; bulk admission acquires pins. | Deterministic IDs allow conflict/reuse, but do not make the referenced input immutable or guarantee downstream publication. |
| Claim | Dirty work atomically changes eligible rows to `running`; chunk claim atomically writes `running`, owner and expiry after request/prerequisite predicates. | Dirty rows have no persisted owner token; chunk ownership is fenced by owner but no monotonic claim generation. |
| Lease | Dirty reclaim treats old `updated_at` as a 15-minute stale boundary; chunks heartbeat owner/expiry; request lease columns are present but not the normal execution fence. | In-process wake locks and timestamps are not durable cross-process claim generations; restart can reclaim stale work. |
| Update | Coalescing rewrites dirty ranges/high waters; projection manifests mutate in place; selected cursor/header and request/chunk conflict paths update their existing IDs. | Update under one key is not an immutable version, and request conflict does not replace every identity/config field. |
| Acknowledge | Component writer can write ack, terminal dirty state and projector watermark in one transaction; broad-search admission can complete dirty work and missing-snapshot admission releases claims. | Acknowledgement can precede physical request-wide publication; standalone completion and compaction paths have different atomicity. |
| Build | Component runners mutate physical serving/base rows. Full selected rebuild deletes then drains batches; chunked summary writes partials; `idempotent-output` writes outside the completion transaction. | A crash can leave partial selected/output rows or physical output beside stale/running control state. |
| Validate | Chunk completion validates component-local count/checksum/metrics; candidate validation checks selected completion, required component manifests, identity/hash/generation/watermarks and represented optional state. | Chunk validation excludes later posting-stat/summary-option finalization and does not itself publish a snapshot. |
| Publish | Successful promotion stores validation, retires same-hash active rows, activates candidate and writes LKG in one transaction; request finalization is a separate later status update. | Derived outputs, promotion and request terminalization are not one transaction; old-hash active state remains active. |
| Pin | Deterministic acquire inserts or increments refcount/expiry and retention unions active, LKG and active pins. | Pin acquisition is used, but terminal release/expiry and row deletion have no production owner. |
| Retire | Promotion retires only same-project/same-review-hash active rows; a broader callable obsolete-retirement helper exists. | The broad helper has no production caller, so old-hash active rows remain protected and are not deletion candidates. |
| Fail | Dirty claims become failed; chunks increment retry and become failed or terminal blocked/quarantined; worker fails superseded/finalization requests. Snapshot failed-marker helper exists. | Candidate validation failure does not invoke the failed marker; request failure does not settle chunks/partials/candidates/pins. |
| Retry | Dirty stale/failed work can be reclaimed; chunks use request/default max attempts and backoff; failed requests are readmitted only with a progressable nonterminal chunk. | Promotion/finalization failure after all chunks complete has no automatic readmission path. |
| Compact | Callable ack compaction converts covered points to a high-water row then deletes points; summary reduction accumulates/deletes source partials; retention advances a table cursor. | Ack compaction has no production caller; summary reduction steps are separate; cursor progress proves neither complete cleanup nor safe deletion. |
| Delete | Explicit request replacement deletes obsolete non-running chunks; full selected rebuild deletes its base/header; summary reduction deletes consumed source partials; retention deletes bounded unprotected rows from eleven final/base tables. | No general deletion exists for terminal dirty/ack/watermark, manifests, pins, requests, chunks, selected headers, accumulators or contribution partials; deletion safety is not inferred. |

### Protection, Supersession, Orphans, And Restart

| State | Current protection or transition | Publication/restart failure behavior | Missing lifecycle proof |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Active | Readers resolve current-hash active state; retention protects every active manifest's physical state. | Promotion retires only same-hash active rows; an old hash can remain active and suppress fresh bootstrap. | Single-active/cross-hash retirement authority and immutable component-state binding. |
| Candidate | Fresh bootstrap creates it; component writes refresh copied state; validation gates promotion. | Validation failure returns `promoted:false`; candidate remains candidate and a failed request with completed chunks is not automatically retried. | Failed/quarantine transition, retry owner, expiry and orphan cleanup. |
| Last-known-good | Promotion points the new active row at the prior same-hash active/LKG; readers and retention can use it. | It is a nullable self-reference without FK; fallback can choose a retired same-hash row. | Referential/version rule, retirement horizon and recovery validation. |
| Failed | Dirty/chunk/request failures have separate statuses and retry rules; snapshot schema/status vocabulary includes failed. | Failed snapshot writer is dormant; finalization failure can leave completed chunks, physical derived writes and candidate state. | Unified failure receipt, rollback/repair and terminal cleanup. |
| Pinned | Active, unreleased, positive-refcount, unexpired pins protect snapshot identity in retention. | Production acquisition has no matching terminal release/expiry sweep; pin protection lacks component/selected state in its union row. | Owner settlement, orphan repair, manifest equality and pin-row retention/delete. |
| Partial | Selected full rebuild can be between reset and completed drain; idempotent chunk output can precede completion; summary accumulator/contribution partials persist. | Restart can retry/reclaim, but reduction upsert, refresh and delete are separate and contribution partials are never removed. | Idempotence receipt, partial visibility fence, failed/superseded cleanup and retention. |
| Superseded | Worker marks older foreground/requestless requests failed and can attach matching requestless chunks before failure. | It does not delete or terminalize candidate, chunks, partials, selected base or pins as one operation. | Supersession cascade, immutable winner identity and retained-history policy. |
| Orphan | Requestless bootstrap chunks can be adopted/released; retention checks active/LKG/pins before final-row deletion. | No FK binds requests/chunks/snapshots/partials and no general lifecycle scan deletes abandoned controls or intermediates. | Complete orphan inventory, lease-safe cleanup, restore receipt and deletion authorization. |
| Restart | Chunk leases expire/reclaim; worker cycle repairs requestless adoption and failed requests; startup probes copy/mutate/restore selected control rows. | Idempotent output and selected drains can be interrupted; startup restoration occurs after a mutation and is not crash-atomic. | Deployed restart capture, repair-completion ledger, crash injection and operator restore validation. |
| Publication failure | Candidate validation/promotion or any derived finalizer can fail after component chunks complete. | Request becomes failed; readmission requires a progressable chunk, so completed-chunk finalization has no automatic retry. | Dedicated finalization job/lease/retry state, rollback boundary and route-readability receipt. |

## US-053 Retention, Recovery, And File Lifecycle Reconciliation

US-053 closes the source trace for control, temporary and file shapes frozen
by US-005, US-006, US-014, US-038, US-039, US-048-US-052 at commit
`184c8e9d716e983825ae0a2edee9797ff3b2dc3c`. Retention, a timestamp or status,
a successful write, a checksum, a cleanup helper, a recovery copy and an
operator instruction remain separate contracts. In particular, an in-process
`finally`, force-delete, connection-temporary table or ready session is not
treated as crash cleanup, bounded retention, deletion safety, recoverability or
proof that a consumer received the bytes.

### US-053 Evidence Boundary

| Boundary | Recorded result |
| --- | --- |
| Source identity | Commit `184c8e9d716e983825ae0a2edee9797ff3b2dc3c`; Ralph's pre-existing timestamp-only `tasks/prd.json` modification remains untouched. |
| Prerequisite | US-052 is complete. US-005/US-006 remain authoritative for judgment controls; US-014 for temporary/file census; US-038/US-039 for startup, operator and backup ownership; US-048-US-052 for output, import, mutation, publication, pin and retention boundaries. |
| Allowed evidence | Exact source paths, serializers, SQL builders, file APIs, schedulers, startup/operator registration, static caller/absence searches and isolated fake/disposable tests. |
| Prohibited evidence | No live/current DuckDB, configured snapshot/query/studio, product server/app/browser/desktop shell, operator backup/restore/reset/recovery, production cleanup, import/export/transfer, worker/projector, migration, benchmark or physical profile ran. |
| State and disposition | Twenty new `LIN-####` rows and exact BGO/DBO/closed-CMF transitions use only US-001 `auditStatus`. `proofCheckState`, `recommendationActionability`, `overallCertification`, runtime status and every storage disposition remain independent and unchanged. Missing cleanup never authorizes deletion. |

### Lifecycle Verb, Ownership, And Failure Trace

| Lifecycle verb | Source-observed behavior | Missing path and operator consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retain / pin / expire | Review pins default to 24 hours and protect active/LKG/pinned snapshots; telemetry retains three days; worker registry retains ten minutes when read; managed logs retain seven date days; terminal transfer sessions prune 24 hours after cleanup eligibility. | Pin release/expiry has no production settlement owner; most controls, PDFs/import inputs, provider records, recovery sidecars, successful promoted assets and downloaded copies have no approved horizon. Named expiry is not a sweep. |
| Clean / archive | Hourly judgment cleanup prunes visibility-acked local rows and drained files; transfer recovery cleans owned temp/promoted artifacts; archive/hard-cleanup services mutate selected database rows. | Cleanup phases have no single durable cycle receipt. Archive does not cascade to source files; hard cleanup omits current file families; malformed promotion metadata can prevent cleanup. |
| Back up / restore | Operator backup checkpoints/snapshots, then copies a database and optional source WAL. Startup recovery preserves database/WAL/pre-repair/manifest artifacts and prunes older groups. | No restore command, checksum/open validation, retention/prune, encryption, desktop placement policy or operator restore drill exists. Direct-final copies can be partial. |
| Replay / repair | Job startup replays completion/outbox evidence, repairs orphan queue state, retries delete-pending files and reclaims leases. DuckDB startup can replay/quarantine WAL and rebuild selected indexed tables. | Bounded one-candidate worker startup, separate phases and narrow repair registries do not prove backlog drain, exactly-once replay, table/file completeness or crash-safe restoration. |
| Export / generate | Backup, recovery sidecars, PDFs, structured/Covidence inputs, transfer artifacts and client CSV/JSON/ZIP outputs are generated under distinct ownership. | A generated path/checksum/status does not freeze later hydration, prove byte completion, establish a consumer receipt or authorize source/artifact cleanup. |
| Transfer / atomically publish | Import upload and promotion-manifest replacement use temp/rename; promoted asset copy uses exclusive create, byte/hash validation and caught-error cleanup. Database commit/history/deltas publish separately. | Most transfer artifacts and ZIPs write direct final paths. File, manifest, session and database publication is not one transaction; download has no lease against expiry cleanup. |
| Delete | Job deletion orders closeout/token/telemetry/job removal and persists local-file delete failures; local SQLite deletion removes database/WAL/SHM/lease. Review retention and transfer cleanup use scoped guards. | No complete reference/orphan scanner or lease-safe cleanup registry spans controls, temp/spill, runtime assets, imports, recovery evidence and client files. State without cleanup remains deletion-unsafe. |

### Control, Temporary, And File Contract Matrix

| Family | Retention/recovery owner and consumer watermark | Partial/orphan protection | Unresolved lifecycle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Central judgment controls | Delete service, hourly cron, three-day telemetry prune, provider-lease reconciliation and 30-second closeout backfill own different rows. | Token-use/closeout/job deletion is ordered; delete-pending preserves local-file failure. | Most job/health/backfill/closeout rows have no age horizon or consumer watermark; deletion/rebuild shape and deployed recovery remain open. |
| Job-local SQLite and worker journal | `lastProjectRefreshAckToken` plus current dirty token gates local outbox/queue pruning; owner acknowledgement gates accepted-claim removal. | Lease, checkpoint, visibility acknowledgement, rollout replay and retained completion evidence protect active work. | No versioned schema ledger, cross-host fence, complete backlog-drain receipt, local backup/restore or approved retained-evidence horizon. |
| Review controls | Active/LKG/pin identities protect final serving; point/high-water acknowledgements and projector watermarks serve projection intake. | Scoped retention excludes protected final rows. | Overlay/search have no operating cleanup; pin settlement, request/chunk/control/partial cleanup and complete consumer-watermark authority remain missing. |
| Migration/runtime temp tables | Transaction/connection lifetime and explicit drop/catch/finally own normal cleanup. | Operation-UUID names reduce collisions; transfer writers drop staged families and connection close drops temp objects. | Nontransactional migration failure, process crash, connection reuse, spill/RSS, disk quota, sensitive residue and applied-ledger/deployed completion are unproved. |
| DuckDB/WAL/temp/snapshot/backup | DuckDB owner/checkpoint, snapshot caller, startup recovery and explicit reset are separate owners. | Snapshot materialization opens the copy; startup recovery retains a selected group. | Direct-final partials, WAL pairing, temp spill, reset safety, backup validation/retention and executable restore remain unresolved. |
| Local JSON/log/lock files | Lease release/takeover, read-triggered registry prune, settings rewrite, log install/date rollover and process shutdown own separate paths. | Exclusive create or atomic temp/rename exists only for selected lease/registry/supervisor paths. | Malformed/direct-write crash behavior, temp siblings, PID reuse, redaction, count-vs-age retention, desktop log cap and approved recovery are missing. |
| PDFs/import/provider/FHIR files | Producer-specific failure cleanup, persisted cursor/reference, PDF reset, provider freshness calculation and FHIR `finally` are separate. | Root/path guards prevent escape; FHIR and known import failures remove their own temp/source file. | File/reference atomicity, success/archive cleanup, partial parallel writes, checksum, orphan scan, provider prune and crash cleanup are absent. |
| Transfer/session/promoted assets | Session owner/heartbeat/recovery, terminal cleanup marker and promotion ownership metadata govern cleanup. | Safe roots, upload rename, ZIP validation, exclusive asset copy/checksum and session-owned deletion guard exist. | Direct-final artifacts, malformed/missing manifest, copy-before-manifest orphan, concurrent download cleanup, successful asset horizon and retained client copy remain open. |
| Recovery sidecars/client files | Operator scripts retain sidecars; browser creates a Blob URL, invokes save and revokes the URL. | Sidecars preserve evidence; server does not claim browser/OS file ownership. | Version/signature/secret policy, stale reapplication, prune, download receipt/integrity, desktop parity and OS retention are outside current ownership. |

### Operator Consequences And Owner Questions Preserved

| Observed action/state | Consequence if treated as stronger evidence | Required owner decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bun run db:backup` reports a path | An operator can receive a partial/unverified database or unmatched WAL and has no executable restore or prune workflow. | Approve backup identity, atomic publication, checksum/open validation, encryption, horizon and restore drill. |
| Local database reset succeeds | Database/WAL/temp/job roots are deleted and migrations recreate empty schema; this is destructive reset, not recovery. | Define authority, preflight backup, confirmation, restore/rollback and deletion receipt. |
| Archive/delete status is terminal | Structured/Covidence/PDF/provider/transfer/recovery files can remain, while current controls and audit evidence have separate owners. | Publish the exhaustive reference/file registry, retention horizons and lease-safe orphan/deletion policy. |
| Transfer session is ready or terminal-cleaned | A ready download can race cleanup; a copied promotion can predate manifest visibility; successful assets can persist indefinitely. | Define download lease/receipt, file/session/database fence, manifest corruption policy and success/failure retention. |
| Cleanup helper or `finally` exists | Process termination can bypass it; direct-final files, temp siblings, connection temp state and OS spool can remain. | Define crash scans, bounded cadence, ownership token, cleanup completion ledger and operator escalation. |
| Client Blob URL is revoked | Revocation releases the in-page URL, not the browser/desktop/OS saved copy; no integrity or retention receipt exists. | Define platform save/integrity behavior and explicitly assign downloaded-copy lifecycle outside server deletion. |

### Identity, Constraint, And Index Reconciliation

| Identity or constraint | Checked-in contract | Missing authority preserved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Data-source/import-route identity | Data source and import route use UUID PKs; route has `UNIQUE(route)`; the bridge has PK, two FKs and unique pair, while production uses the denormalized `data_source.import_route` string. | Bridge ownership, denormalized/relational authority, route deactivation/archive cascade and deployed constraint equality. |
| Cursor identity | Structured/Covidence configs carry `kind` and `version=1`; other producers persist opaque strings or rooted paths in the same VARCHAR. | One versioned tagged union, legacy/extra-key policy, progress reset/replay semantics and file/reference equality. |
| Article identity | `app.article.id` is canonical PK; legacy `article_id` is nullable/non-unique; strong identifiers are unique by `(kind,normalized_value)`; source-record identity is separate. | Source precedence, merge/delete/race transaction, identifier cleanup, deployed collisions and compatibility horizon. |
| Import identity | Current link is unique by article/route; source record is unique by route/source key. External ID, run ID, raw hash and metadata do not replace either key. | Stale synchronization across all import families, history/quarantine retention, raw schema/equality and replay after late membership. |
| Project identity | Project PK, direct project/article unique pair and project/import-route unique pair are separate. Project-side FKs were removed; subproject has no parent/source discriminator. | Orphan policy, subproject provenance, delete/restore authority and project/route/direct precedence. |
| Physical scope identity | `mart.project_scope_article` has PK `(project_id,article_id)` plus curated/route booleans and article timestamps. | Immutable input version, incremental-vs-rebuild publication contract, project/article FKs, retention and row-level deployed equality. |
| Named index set | Fourteen in-scope index rows cover legacy article lookup, current/source import directions, project deletion/membership directions, tombstone cleanup and canonical quarantine/identifier lookup. | Approved deployed existence, optimizer plans, selectivity, size/write cost, rebuild completion and redundancy decisions. |

### Identity, Constraint, Hash, And Invalidation Reconciliation

| Contract | Checked-in identity or rule | Missing authority preserved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prompt identity | UUID PK; nullable unique content hash; current immutable writer hashes original/transformed/heading/type; review hash falls back to SHA-256 of original text when content hash is null; transfer recomputes the current content hash. | Legacy-null migration/reuse, cross-hash equivalence, collision/merge policy, direct-repair null hash, recovery and retention. |
| Project-prompt identity | Unique project/prompt pair plus independent link ID, order, enabled/archive state, origin project and criteria metadata. Only prompt has a final FK. | Criteria/hash/delta inclusion, project/origin orphan policy, state applicability, clone/repair/transfer parity and index physical value. |
| Stored versus selectable model | Stored model PK and unique provider/remote/`COALESCE(variant,'')` index are distinct from virtual Codex/Anthropic selectable IDs that can be materialized later. | Null remote-ID semantics, virtual/stored stability, provider deletion/rebind, natural-key remap and execution/judgment identity. |
| Provider/config identity | Provider PK is the only DB constraint. Provider kind, auth mode, endpoint, config, secret, enablement, health and concurrency are independently nullable/unconstrained where declared. | Closed enums/JSON schema, endpoint/secret validation, positive concurrency, redaction/restore, runtime alias and enablement invalidation policy. |
| Review-config hash | Human mode, model ID/execution options/provider connection-kind-base/remote/variant, active prompt hashes/order and four content flags are hashed in two current readers. | One authoritative implementation/version, criteria and legacy-hash policy, excluded provider/model fields, mutable-manifest behavior and immutable consumer fence. |
| Scope/date/route | Curated and selected-route membership are unioned; dates are inclusive and nullable; route handlers reject inverted ranges. Selected-import ID omits review/date/route state while serving snapshots also carry review hash/watermarks. | One applicability rule, route/direct precedence, reset/range reuse, late membership replay, DB/transfer checks and immutable scope publication. |
| Delta/invalidation | Prompt changes use prompt-scoped rebuild; project config starts a component rebuild at project scope; model/provider repository changes fan out to projects as model-execution changes. | Direct-writer parity, exact field completeness, comparison/transfer invalidation, readmission after completed-chunk finalization failure and current-hash repair admission. |
| Execution snapshot | Judgment execution payload freezes broader project dates/flags, selected route/source, prompt, provider/model and article content with its own SHA-256 identity. | Required versus incidental dimensions, secret/config redaction, current-row drift, job retry/reuse and export/transfer equality. |

legacy review-state, assessment, token-accounting, execution-snapshot,
DuckDB import-marker, per-job SQLite outbox and judge-worker completion objects
at commit `5556f1d392869ab9c124cb77df2ec4b3baf11f12`. The exact primary
scope is `DBO-0032`-`DBO-0061` and
`CMF-0209`-`CMF-0433`: 12 table/catalog objects, 16 named indexes,
two file containers, 189 physical columns and 36 material JSON/key-family rows.

reconciliation-terminal as `blocked`. This is not a storage disposition.
`proofCheckState`, `recommendationActionability`,
`overallCertification`, lineage/runtime state and every provisional
recommendation remain independent and unchanged. No object is called
authoritative, obsolete, movable or deletable. Missing deployed values,
approved physical measurements and immutable benchmark/runtime captures remain
explicitly pending for Phase 4.

### Identity, Constraint, Serializer, And Lifecycle Reconciliation

| Contract | Checked-in identity or rule | Missing authority preserved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Active LLM truth | Product reads use article/prompt/model/four content flags plus `deleted_at IS NULL`. Physical uniqueness adds `delete_generation` and cannot express active-only uniqueness. | One authoritative generation/tombstone rule across direct, batch, import, transfer, prompt merge/delete, project cleanup and admin paths; deployed duplicate values and collision recovery. |
| Human prompt truth | Unique project/article/prompt row with independent pending/answered/answer/comment fields. Blank optional submission marks answered without the same delta/overlay path as nonblank submission. | Blank-answer semantics, old/new prompt identity, delete tombstone kind, late membership, reviewer overlay settlement and comparison invalidation equality. |
| Human summary, legacy review and assessment | Summary is project/article/origin; legacy review is project/article with section flags/comments; assessment is unique per LLM judgment. | Which surface is authoritative in every mode, ordinary writer completeness, stale field retirement, transfer merge policy and lifecycle/retention. |
| Token truth | Row identity is independent from nullable job ID. Aggregate, success/failure and request-attempt fields are separately serialized and can be rebuilt. | Exact counter algebra, attempt deduplication, closed JSON/version domain, failed closeout, direct backfill receipts, orphan policy and durable retention. |
| Execution snapshot | Unique job/queue/claim, separate UUID, version-2 payload and SHA-256. `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` can retain the pre-existing row. | Conflict hash equality/failure rule, remap of embedded relational IDs, retry/reuse/transient parity, immutable consumer fence and retention. |
| Local job outbox | Per-file AUTOINCREMENT sequence plus job/queue/judgment/claim/snapshot identities and export lease fields. Central marker uses job/outbox sequence. | Versioned schema ledger, lease/fencing across hosts, canonical insertion receipt, crash window, replay order, sequence reset/repair and safe file cleanup. |
| Worker completion journal | Claim-centered completion evidence and request-attempt-centered pending token evidence use different keys; legacy repair can synthesize evidence. | Exactly-once ACK/application proof, local-applied semantics, accepted-claim equality, corruption/version repair receipt, startup backlog bound and file ownership. |
| Projected review truth | LLM/Human status, queue, payload/detail, posting, summary, overlays and comparison cells derive and publish separately. | One consumer watermark, atomic/current snapshot visibility, overlay read/reconcile/expiry ownership, comparison freshness and completed-finalization readmission. |

### Route, Runtime, Writer, Projector, Replay, Repair, Retention, Export, Transfer, Benchmark, Startup, Script, And Non-Production Trace

| Evidence plane | Exact checked-in result | Remaining blocker |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Routes and shared UI | Product composition mounts Human assessment, token, judgment-job, article and project routes; shared Solid code issues Human init/submit/refetch and consumes review/token/detail results. | Source mount and query keys do not prove actual browser/desktop request order, caching, navigation, hash routing, values or rendering. |
| Runtime writers | Direct judge, batch append, SQLite import, Human init/submit, Covidence, project/prompt/admin cleanup, token storage/rebuild and transfer target writers touch different subsets. | Transaction equality, every writer's generation/delta/comparison/transfer invalidation, deployed invocation and failed-closeout behavior. |
| Projectors and readers | Status, queue, payload/detail, posting, summary, comparison, article/project detail and current-table fallbacks read different truth objects. | Component acknowledgement is not one physical mutation or immutable publication; current-table hydration can drift after candidate/snapshot selection. |
| Replay and repair | Local importer separates central transaction from local ACK; worker journal replays completion evidence; startup and operator scripts repair selected legacy/local states. | Durable cross-store transaction, exact crash matrix, one recovery ledger, bounded backlog, lease uniqueness, corruption handling and operator completion receipt. |
| Startup | Runtime profile/role controls migrations, job recovery and judge-worker cleanup. The worker startup path performs a bounded initial replay before later loop processing. | Actual supported-role restart, backlog drain, socket/runtime availability, crash injection and terminal cleanup were not observed. |
| Retention and files | Local prune/checkpoint/delete code and archived/job cleanup cover named tables/files; serving retention excludes source review truth. | Scheduled invocation, reader lease, retention horizons, reference/orphan scans, concurrent cleanup, restore validation and durable cleanup receipts. |
| Export | CSV selection uses serving snapshot payload/detail; later job/download paths can hydrate current data. | Frozen selection versus hydration equality, integrity, concurrent-download lease, cleanup and retained-copy lifecycle. |
| Transfer | Canonical LLM/Human/summary/review/assessment rows are packaged and remapped; token/snapshot/outbox rows are not package members. | Package omission is not deletion authority; target conflict policy, invalidation settlement, rollback, integrity and source/target retained lifecycle are unresolved. |
| Benchmark | Review-serving and transfer benchmarks exercise synthetic source-defined shapes. | Approved fixture, seed, model/provider/thinking/prompt/content/memory/runtime values, complete instrumentation and physical measurements are absent. |
| Scripts and package commands | SQLite import/repair and serving cutover commands are exposed; other checked-in repair/backfill/recovery scripts are direct entrypoints with different guards. | Command presence or maintenance-access guards do not prove authorization, deployed copy, invocation history, recovery completion or storage disposition. |
| Tests and fixtures | Focused schema, writer, projector, route, lifecycle, transfer and script tests use mocks or disposable databases. | Synthetic results do not establish deployed schema/data/plans, physical cost, browser/desktop behavior, crash recovery or operator use. |

### Discovery-Surface Closure

| Search surface | Result |
| --- | --- |
| DuckDB migrations and runtime rebuilds | Full-file-name lexical order was applied through final rebuilds; bootstrap FKs/indexes were not treated as current when later files remove or recreate them. The token runtime rebuild was compared with migration shape. |
| SQLite base/runtime/catalog shape | Base CREATEs, every add-column/index/partial-index helper, required-schema checks, implicit AUTOINCREMENT catalog and legacy repair were mapped. No versioned deployed-shape ledger or approved immutable file exists. |
| Qualified names, aliases and generated SQL | `app.*`, unqualified transaction names, schema aliases, generated insert/select lists, JSON helpers and route/projector payload mappings were searched and linked to the primary manifest rows. |
| Routes, registries and consumers | Product route composition, route inventory, component/invalidation/retention registries, service imports, Solid query keys and visible response fields were checked. Registry presence is not invocation proof. |
| Scripts and package exposure | Package commands and all matching direct scripts were checked separately. Exposure, checked-in presence and deployed operator use remain distinct. |
| Export and transfer | Durable selection, current hydration, transfer payload schemas, target analysis/commit and fidelity validation were distinguished. Source absence from a package is not retention/deletion evidence. |
| Tests, fixtures, tasks and plans | Exact references were labeled non-production. Broad matches were resolved to source symbols or retained as missing evidence; no fixture value was adopted as benchmark-critical configuration. |
| Negative searches | No ordinary non-transfer writer was found for all legacy review/assessment fields; no transfer serialization was found for token, execution-snapshot or local outbox/journal rows; no source-truth entry was found in serving-table retention. These are checked-in-source observations only. |

## US-057 Judgment-Job And Execution-Control Object Reconciliation

US-057 terminally reconciles the complete US-006 judgment-job and
execution-control census at commit
`b752907b1beb290c9cde8dd380b64764ccfbb903`. The exact primary scope is
`DBO-0062`-`DBO-0093` and `CMF-0434`-`CMF-0661`: eight DuckDB tables, five
per-job SQLite tables, one judge-worker SQLite table, 16 current named
indexes, two JSON lock/lease files, 201 physical columns and 27 material
JSON/file-key families.

All 32 primary DBO rows and all 228 primary CMF rows are now
reconciliation-terminal as `blocked`. This is not a storage disposition.
Runtime job, queue, lease, attempt, retry, import, health and result states
remain separate from `auditStatus`; `proofCheckState`,
`recommendationActionability`, `overallCertification`, lineage/runtime state
and every provisional recommendation remain independent and unchanged. No
object is called authoritative, obsolete, movable or deletable. Missing
deployed values, supported recovery observations and approved physical
measurements remain explicitly pending for Phase 4.

### Identity, State, Constraint, Serializer, And Lifecycle Reconciliation

| Contract | Checked-in identity or transition | Missing authority preserved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Job and project | Job PK is application UUID; route checks for an existing project job before insert, but SQL has no unique project key. Creation inserts `running`; route/service types still retain `not_started`. Job and storage status are unchecked strings with separate import/pause/quarantine/tuning/cursor fields. | One authoritative natural identity, race fence, initial-state rule, complete status/storage/import transition graph, history, recovery and retention. |
| Scan, queue and admission | Scan cursor/date/article/prompt/bucket/epoch advances separately from SQLite insertion; queue identity is unique job/article/prompt, while ready order, claim ID and execution snapshot are later bindings. | Cursor-to-insert accounting, duplicate/filter rejection receipts, authoritative status/terminal/retry vocabulary, exact queue claim fence and supported restart behavior. |
| Claim, execution, retry and result | Accepted claim uses claim ID plus relational job/queue columns and a JSON prompt payload; claim conflict replaces only payload/time. Retry clears claim/snapshot and assigns a new ready sequence. Completion-ACK conflict fills only token/attempt evidence; local outbox, central import marker, canonical judgment and visibility ACK are separate durable facts. | Relational/payload equality, conflict identity, exactly-once execution/result/import/visibility settlement, replay order, stale-result rejection and terminal retention. |
| Request attempt and closeout | Manifest entry, provider admission identity, durable closeout PK `(request_attempt_id,provider_key)`, completion copies and token evidence are distinct. Conflict keeps the earliest closeout/time/token tuple. | Authoritative attempt version, CAS/late-conflict semantics, provider diagnostic domain, missing/duplicate closeout repair and retention. |
| Maintenance/provider/local leases | Maintenance ID composes work/scope/optional entity IDs; provider identity encodes request or probe; per-job lease and worker lock use host/process metadata. | Cross-process/cross-host uniqueness, clock/expiry authority, fencing token history, failover ordering and reader-safe file ownership. |
| Backfill and scheduler | Singleton ID is conventional; high-water, cursor, counters, errors and completion are persisted. Production scheduler is maintenance-owner only, delayed 30 seconds, five-by-1,000 bounded and suppressed at `DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT <= 6400MiB`. | Whether suppressed deployments ever complete closeout repair, terminal retry/error policy, operator receipt, temporary-state cleanup and backfill retention. |
| Health and telemetry | Health overwrites by job and expires by freshness; telemetry appends by UUID with unique job/provider/cadence and three-day code pruning. | Authoritative freshness/topology/aggregation version, removed-index intent, JSON redaction, retained horizon and equality between health, telemetry and runtime state. |
| Audit state | Runtime values above remain product data. US-057 changes only manifest `auditStatus` to `blocked`. | Proof, actionability, certification, runtime state and storage disposition cannot be inferred from one another. |

### Identity, State, Constraint, And Index Reconciliation

| Contract | Checked-in behavior | Missing authority preserved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Delta identity | `review-serving-delta:<sha256>` idempotency hashes source mutation key, operation, partition, row/table and typed key; `delta:<sha256-prefix>` derives from that key. PK and unique idempotency are separate constraints. | Collision/equivalence policy, typed-key/payload/relational equality, source-mutation completeness, deployed conflicts and retention horizon. |
| Source high-water | A row keyed by source partition is inserted if absent, incremented and read before a new delta/outbox insert; duplicate delta lookup occurs before allocation. | Authoritative partition registry, multi-writer fence, committed-gap semantics, allocator/reconciliation coupling and deployed monotonicity. |
| Delta reconciliation | Intake validates payload version/kind/required keys, fans out dirty work and stamps `reconciled_at`; valid zero-membership rows can be stamped with zero dirty work. | Later-membership replay, acknowledgement equivalence, physical publication fence, failure readmission and safe pruning watermark. |
| Outbox recovery | `outbox:<sha256-prefix>` shares the delta idempotency identity; recovery minimally checks discriminator, change kind, mutation key and record typed key, then reuses the allocated high-water. | Production producer, claimant/lease fence, scheduler/retry bound, operator-terminal authorization, full versioned schema, drain receipt and retention. |
| Cursor control state | PK is `source_partition`; source allocation mutates high-water/updated time and diagnostics reads quarantine. | Writers for last reconciled delta, status, lease, retry, error and quarantine; transition/check constraints; relationship to delta/outbox/projector watermarks. |
| Hot-fact identity | PK `(import_route_id,article_id,source_record_key)` is separate from source-record hash/run/current-link identity. Rank key combines normalized numeric priority, article and source key. | Canonical current/history precedence, remap/undelete behavior, full backfill/rebuild, raw/typed equality, late membership and retention. |
| Dynamic registry identity | Fourteen change kinds map to required keys, update modes and component topology; hot columns map separately to ranking/display/filter/posting/contribution roles. | SQL-enforced vocabulary, registry/deployed-version synchronization, consumer-complete field authority and safe registry evolution. |
| Named index set | Six delta indexes, one outbox status index and two hot-fact indexes are current checked-in declarations. | Applied existence, optimizer plans/use, selectivity/cardinality, bytes/write cost, rebuild completion and redundancy decisions. |

### Identity, Lease, State, Key, And Index Reconciliation

| Contract | Checked-in behavior | Missing authority preserved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dirty identity/coalescing | `dirtyWork:<digest>` hashes the serialized component/identity plus dirty kind, project, scope, partition and optional projection key; high water, ranges and latest delta are mutable under that row. Conflict widens bounds, resets `pending` and refreshes `updated_at`. | Collision/equivalence rules, immutable input version, concurrent-upsert versus active-claim behavior, deployed duplicates and history. |
| Dirty claim/lease | One atomic update selects the oldest eligible component lane/partition/identity and writes `running`; stale `running` and `failed` rows become eligible after 15 minutes. Release/fail/complete guard only on status. | Persisted owner, lease expiry, monotonic attempt/generation, heartbeat, compare-and-set completion, error/attempt history and exact affected-row accounting. |
| Point ACK | `dirtyAck:<digest>` includes dirty ID, component/identity, partition and claim high water. Upsert replay checks any completed ACK with sufficient high water and covering range; completion inserts ACK before a status-guarded dirty update. | Stale-owner exclusion, ACK-to-successful-transition proof, point/range authority, source/delta/publication equality, orphan rules and exact replay fence. |
| High-water compaction | Compaction hashes the requested completed high water into the ACK ID, upserts that row, then deletes covered point rows while excluding every null-link high-water row. | A single monotonic per-lane cursor does not result across distinct thresholds. Scheduling, superseded-receipt cleanup, crash transaction boundary, consumer proof and evidence horizon are absent. |
| Project-import cursor | Compound PK is project/import route; status, high water, cursor, lease, retry/error and timestamps have migration defaults only. Its named index starts with import route. | Production applicability, serializer/version, claim/advance/retry/replay/repair state machine, owner and index intent. |
| Projector watermark | Application ID includes projector/project/route/component/partition, while the final table does not enforce it. Update-then-insert uses only an in-process lock; startup can inspect/dedupe IDs. | Cross-process uniqueness/CAS, coherent duplicate merge, reader authority, relationship to ACK/manifest/snapshot state and ownership of generation/patch/snapshot/status/lease/cursor/error fields. |
| Projection input scalar/map | Component writers replace a scalar plus map derived from claim source prefixes/aliases; selected-import and rebuild paths can seed different subsets. Promotion/diagnostics compare snapshot requirements through duplicated component registries. | Canonical keys/aliases, component override precedence, numeric/range/scalar coherence, closed serializer/migration version, clean/upgrade equivalence and immutable publication binding. |
| Named indexes | Dirty lookup, ACK component and project-cursor route indexes are the three current names. Claim predicates/order do not lead with the dirty index columns; the cursor index has no production predicate. | Applied existence, optimizer plan/use, cardinality/selectivity, bytes/write cost, rebuild history and necessity/redundancy decisions. |

### Writer, Reader, Registry, Projector, Replay, And Repair Reconciliation

| Evidence plane | Exact checked-in result | Remaining blocker |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dirty producers | Review/import delta intake uses the 14-kind invalidation registry to create component rows; projector repair can also upsert. Acknowledged ranges can suppress re-creation. | Static coverage cannot prove every source event, late membership and repair path yields the exact eventual component/input set or that ACK suppression equals visible publication. |
| Claims and runners | The maintenance worker performs delta intake, then claims 11 components in dependency order. In-memory retries reuse one claim set; failures/releases mutate status only, without an owner token. | Multi-process claimant fencing, stale-runner side-effect exclusion, durable retry/error accounting and bounded deployed backlog remain unproved. |
| Normal component completion | The shared writer can transact output statements/records, mutable projection manifests, point ACKs and projector source high water. Only the final snapshot in multi-snapshot loops normally acknowledges. | Per-component atomicity does not prove request-wide/cross-component visibility, immutable manifest input, snapshot promotion, exact row-result accounting or later safe compaction. |
| Exceptional completion | Broad project search acknowledges after rebuild admission; missing snapshots release/fail claims; payload with no compatible snapshot completes claims without a payload manifest/watermark. Standalone completion and exported completion-plus-watermark helpers differ from shared-writer paths. | Local `completed`/ACK does not uniformly mean physical output, accepted rebuild, watermark, immutable candidate or active/LKG visibility. Recovery and replay rules differ by branch. |
| Persisted projector watermark | The outbox barrier is read before source progress advance; the physical row is otherwise not a product/diagnostic freshness input. Promotion uses projection-manifest scalar/map state instead. | A successful write cannot prove any durable consumer observed it, duplicate rows agree, or it safely fences delta/outbox/ACK cleanup. |
| Projection input readers | Manifest repository, worker/rebuild paths, promotion and diagnostics consume scalar/map values. The snapshot-based operator inspector exposes the scalar only. | Registry duplication, unvalidated dynamic maps, omitted operator map visibility and mutable manifest keys prevent authoritative freshness/replay certification. |
| Project-import cursor | Exact production closure reaches only the migration; schema tests and old plans reference it. | No operating writer, reader, claimant, replay, repair, startup, cleanup or script lifecycle exists in checked-in production code. |
| Diagnostics | Diagnostics reads dirty status/ages and projection-manifest input watermarks, but not ACK rows, the project-import cursor or persisted projector-watermark rows. It hardcodes dirty failed count to zero. | Mutable counts are observations, not claims, ACKs, watermarks, replay receipts or cleanup fences; browser/desktop request behavior was not observed. |

### Startup, Retention, Script, And Non-Production Closure

| Surface | Checked-in closure | Unsupported inference retained |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runtime scheduling | Maintenance-role background composition starts the supervised projector heartbeat; pause/recovery and memory-bounded restart paths can defer or recycle work. | Source wiring and passing fake-clock tests do not prove deployed cadence, exclusive owner topology, backlog bounds or recovery completion. |
| Startup probe/repair | Indexed-table repair specs count/probe dirty, ACK and watermark rows. Watermark repair intentionally does not recreate a key/index; the project cursor and projection manifest are omitted. Probe mutation and restoration use separate transactions. | Invocation does not prove crash-safe restoration, coherent duplicate repair, retained artifact integrity, successful deployed repair or operator restore validation. |
| Retention/cleanup | The rotating bounded registry deletes only eleven final/selected tables. No dirty/cursor/watermark/manifest delete exists; ACK point deletion exists only inside the unscheduled compactor. | Missing cleanup is not safe-retention or deletion authority. Consumer watermark, reference/orphan scan, reader lease, bounded horizon, durable receipt, backup and restore proof remain absent. |
| Package/direct scripts | Rebuild request commands admit later work; the snapshot inspector reads manifest scalar watermarks. No command directly owns claim repair, ACK compaction, project-cursor recovery, projector-watermark reconciliation or primary retention. | Command exposure/absence cannot establish authorization, deployed invocation, recovery completion, portability intent or safe retirement. |
| Tests/fixtures/plans | Unit/integration tests exercise current mechanics; migrations use disposable `/tmp` databases; a script helper can insert projection manifests; old CQRS/OOM plans describe intended cursor/watermark roles. | Synthetic/disposable and historical evidence cannot establish deployed shape/values, actual worker concurrency, operator behavior, physical cost or lifecycle authority. |
| Negative searches | Exact names, aliases, field symbols, IDs, indexes, compactor and SQL verbs were searched across source, scripts, migrations, tests, tasks and plans. | Checked-in absence does not prove generated/deployed absence, invocation history, authorization, safe deletion or final disposition. |
